3. Agricultural forest land
To be classified as agricultural forest, land must meet the criteria under state law (sec . 70 .32(2)(c)1d ., Wis . Stats .) .
Agricultural forest land:
• Must be producing or capable of producing commercial forest products
• Must be contiguous to a parcel that is classified in its entirety as agricultural
• Must be owned by the same person who owns the contiguous parcel classified entirely as agricultural
• Agricultural forest land and the agricultural parcel can only be separated by a road
Review the Agricultural Assessment Guide for agricultural forest examples .
IX. Presentation of Evidence
A. Presumption of correctness
After the assessor’s affidavit is completed and signed, the BOR must accept the valuations in the assessment roll as
correct valuations . According to state law, the BOR must presume the assessor’s valuation is correct . This presumption
of correctness is binding on the BOR unless sufficient evidence to the contrary exists . To overturn this presumption of
correctness, the property owner has the burden of proof to show evidence proving the assessor is incorrect .
B. Evidence available to the BOR
The BOR can only consider the sworn oral testimony of witnesses appearing before it . Courts have held that if
appropriate credible evidence is presented to the BOR showing the assessor’s valuation to be incorrect, the BOR
must consider it .
A BOR can request additional evidence . If the BOR or the assessor request, the BOR can compel witnesses to appear
for questioning . The law allows ill or disabled objectors to testify by phone if a letter from a physician, surgeon or
osteopath confirms their illness or disability . The municipality must pay for the call .
In addition to oral testimony, the BOR can also subpoena books, records, appraisals, documents and any other data
that may help to understand the issue . If the objector’s or the assessor’s used the income approach for valuation,
the objection should not be heard unless the objector supplies to the assessor all the necessary income and
expense information the assessor requests .
The assessor must give the BOR any information relating to the appealed assessment . In addition, the assessor
should prepare to present the facts and valuation methods used to develop the assessments . The information
presented should help the BOR determine if the assessment is correct . The objection form may contain written
testimony or contain exhibits to become part of the BOR proceedings .
If evidence is submitted that was only available to one side prior to the hearing, the BOR should request
documentation of any evidence submitted that has not been proven . If documentation is unavailable, this should
impact the BOR’s evaluation of the credibility of the evidence .
The BOR must provide adequate time for the property owner and the assessor to present their information .
C. All testimony must be given under oath
BOR considers sworn oral testimony of witnesses appearing before the BOR
• Only evidence given under oath is binding
• The BOR is required to hear upon oath, by telephone, all ill or disabled persons who present to the board a letter
from a physician, osteopath, physician assistant, or advanced practice nurse prescriber that confirms their illness
or disability

2026 Guide for Board of Review Members
• In addition to sworn oral testimony, an objector must also specify in writing, the person’s (ex: property owner)
estimate of the land value and improvements that are the subject of the objection . The objector must also
specify the information the person used to arrive at that estimate .
• BOR may accept sworn information over the telephone or a sworn written statement:
» DOR created – Request to Testify by Telephone or Submit a Sworn Written Statement (PA-814)
» BOR determines whether it will accept information in writing or over the phone
» BOR reviews requests during the first meeting of the BOR
» Property owner must provide the 48-hour notice of intent to appeal
» Property owner must complete the objection form
» Considerations – written information does not allow for cross examination, audibility for information over the
phone, identification of speakers
• BOR may also postpone and reschedule a hearing – limited to once during the same session for the same property
X. BOR Decisions
A. Reaching a decision
After the BOR hears all the evidence, it must deliberate to reach a decision . The deliberation process is open to the public .
BOR deliberates in one of these ways:
• After each objection is heard
• After all objections are heard
• Periodically during the time the BOR is open
After hearing all the evidence, the BOR determines if the assessor’s valuation is correct . The BOR’s decision should
incorporate the understanding that the assessor is presumed correct and the objector has the burden of proof to
sufficiently show the assessment is incorrect . DOR recommends recording the deliberation discussion and final
determination . The BOR’s determination is by roll call vote . Decisions to adjust assessments need to clearly identify
the final assessment allocated to the land and the improvements .
B. End of BOR hearing
1. Notification needed at the end of a BOR hearing
The BOR may announce its decision to the property owner and assessor at the conclusion of the hearing, or it
may take the case under advisement . However, the BOR clerk must provide the objector, or the appropriate party,
notice of the finalized assessment before the final adjournment . This written notice must also explain the property
owner’s appeal rights and procedures . The BOR clerk must also prepare an affidavit that includes the date the
notice was delivered or mailed .
2. Clerk’s responsibility after the BOR makes its decisions
The clerk should summarize the proceedings and decisions on DOR prescribed form (PA-800) .
Summary should include the following:
• Property owner’s name
• Property description
• Amount of the objected assessment
• Names of the persons who appeared for the property owner
• BOR determination
The municipality should keep this form for at least seven years with the clerk’s notes, written objections and all
other material submitted to the BOR .

If a property owner is not satisfied with the BOR decision, there are three appeal options available . There are filing
requirements for each appeal option . For more detailed information review the Guide for Property Owners .
If a property owner did not contest the assessment before the local BOR, no other reviewing authority will hear the
property owner’s case .
A. Appeal options
• Appealing to DOR – sec . 70 .85, Wis . Stats .
• Appealing to the circuit court – sec . 70 .47(13), Wis . Stats .
• Appealing to the municipality (excessive assessment) – sec . 74 .37, Wis . Stats .
1. Appealing to DOR
A property owner can file a written complaint with the DOR Equalization Supervisor . This appeal has several conditions .

Wisconsin law declares it public policy that all persons are entitled to the greatest possible information regarding the affairs of
government. Public records shall be presumed open. Denial of access is generally contrary to the public interest and may only occur
in exceptional cases. — Wis. Stat. § 19.31

Custodian

LOCATION OF RECORDS

ACCESS HOURS & ADVANCE NOTICE
Regular access period: Mondays, 10:00 AM – 1:00 PM
24-hour advance written or oral notice required to inspect or
copy records during this period. — Wis. Stat. § 19.34(2)(b)2.
Outside access period: contact clerk to schedule an
appointment; access permitted upon 48 hours’ written or
oral notice. — Wis. Stat. § 19.34(2)(b)1.
Electronic records available by email where practicable — no
appointment needed.
COPY FEES
Fees shall not exceed the actual, necessary, and direct cost of
reproduction. — Wis. Stat. § 19.35(3)(a)
Fee schedule subject to adoption by Town Board and can be
found at www.winchesterwi.com.
Fees may be waived or reduced where the custodian
determines waiver is in the public interest. — Wis. Stat. §
19.35(3)(e)
No fee for inspection that does not involve copying.
LIMITATIONS ON ACCESS
Access may be limited only where: (1) a state or federal
statute exempts the record; (2) a court has established a
common law limitation; or (3) the public interest in
withholding clearly outweighs the public interest in
disclosure. Any denial will be provided in writing with the
specific legal basis stated. — Wis. Stat. §§ 19.35–19.36
HOW TO SUBMIT A REQUEST
Requesters are not required to identify themselves or state the
purpose of a request. — Wis. Stat. § 19.35(1)(i)
• In person at Town Hall during access hours or by
appointment
• Email: clerk@winchester.wi.gov
• Mail: Town Clerk, 7228 CTH W, Winchester WI 54557
• Phone: 715-686-2123
• Online form at winchesterwi.com (encouraged, not required)
Note: While submission via the online form is not required, the
Clerk’s Office will generate an internal electronic request record
for tracking and recordkeeping purposes for every request received,
regardless of how it is submitted. Records will be delivered
electronically unless the requester specifies otherwise.
RESPONSE STANDARD
The custodian shall, as soon as practicable and without delay,
either fill the request or notify the requester of the determination
to deny, in whole or in part, and the reasons therefor. — Wis. Stat.
§ 19.35(4)(a)
Note: While 10 business days is not a statutory deadline, the
Clerk’s Office will make every best effort to respond within that
timeframe. If a request cannot be fulfilled within 10 business days,
the requester will be notified with an explanation and an estimated
completion date.
Records may not be destroyed after a request is received until the
request is fulfilled, or at least 60 days after denial. — Wis. Stat. §
19.35(5)
REMEDIES FOR WRONGFUL DENIAL
A requester who believes access has been wrongfully denied may:
(1) bring a mandamus action in circuit court; or (2) request the
District Attorney or Attorney General to bring such action. —
Wis. Stat. § 19.37(1)
If the requester prevails, the court shall award reasonable attorney
fees, damages of not less than $100, and other actual costs. — Wis.
Stat. § 19.37(2)(a)

IMPORTANT FINANCE CHARGE INFORMATION
We figure the finance charge on your account by applying the daily periodic rate to the "average daily balance" of your account (including current transactions). To get the "average
daily balance" we take the beginning balance of your account each day, add any new advances/loans, and subtract any payments or credits. This gives us the daily balance. Then, we
add up all the daily balances for the billing cycle and divide the total by the number of days in the billing cycle. This gives us the "average daily balance". Late payment fees,
membership fee, annual fee and unpaid finance charges are not included in the calculation of the "average daily balance".

IMPORTANT NOTICE AND CHANGE IN TERMS
CHANGE IN TERMS EFFECTIVE AUGUST 1, 2026
This Important Notice (“Notice”) identifies changes to Section 3, Section 4, Section 5, Section 6, Section 8, Section 10,
Section 12, Section 13 and Section 15 of your Deposit Account Agreement.
• In Section 3.1—we are clarifying the definition of “applicable law” to include applicable federal and state laws, the
UCC, payment network and clearinghouse rules, OFAC sanctions and regulations.
• In Section 4.11—we are revising the Organization Account section to improve clarity regarding authorized
representatives.
• In Section 5.4—we are adding a separate section for terms regarding Remotely Created Checks.
• In Section 5.5—we are adding terms for the receipt of Instant Payments and other payment orders.
• In Section 6—we are revising the stop payment terms to clarify their applicability to checks and identify that other
terms apply to other types of transactions.
• In Section 8—we are revising the error reporting terms to clarify the scope and identify types of transactions that are
subject to different error reporting provisions.
• In Section 8.4—we are adding terms regarding use of Fraud Services such as Positive Pay and ACH Filters for
business customers.
• In Section 10—we are revising the Overdraft terms to improve clarity.
• In Section 12—we are updating the Electronic Fund Transfer terms to clarify applicability to consumer accounts only.
• In Section 13—we are adding wire transfer terms, which also apply to ACH entries and other payment orders
involving business accounts.
• In Section 15.6—we are clarifying the Liability Limitation provisions.
• In Section 15.7—we are adding an Indemnification provision.
• In Section 15.8—we are clarifying the Bank’s rights to take action, including placing freezes and holds and blocking
or delaying transactions in order to prevent losses or reduce risk, such as when there
is suspected fraud or illegal activity or disputes regarding authority to access an account.
• In Section 15.9—we are adding a jury trial waiver and venue provision for business Accounts since they are
excluded from the arbitration provision.
We encourage you to keep a copy of this Notice with your Deposit Account Agreement. For the full Deposit Account
Agreement, visit us online at AssociatedBank.com/Forms or stop by your local Associated Bank. If you have
questions, please contact our Midwest-based Customer Care team at 800-236-8866.

add up all the daily balances for the billing cycle and divide the total by the number of days in the billing cycle. This gives us the "average daily balance". Late payment fees,
membership fee, annual fee and unpaid finance charges are not included in the calculation of the "average daily balance".

Town of Winchester — Address/Fire Number Sign Policy
Policy 2026-04 — Page 2
1. Purpose
This policy establishes the procedure for the issuance, installation, replacement, and fee
structure of address/fire number signs within the Town of Winchester, ensuring that all
properties are clearly and uniformly marked to support emergency response and mail/delivery
services.
2. Eligibility & Requests
• Any member of the public may request an address/fire number sign for a property
within the Town of Winchester.
• An address/fire number sign is issued only after an address number has been assigned by
Vilas County.
3. Issuance & Installation Process
The following process applies to the issuance and installation of all address/fire number signs:
• The Vilas County Clerk assigns the address number and notifies the Town Clerk.
• The Town Clerk orders the sign through Lange Signs, using the Town’s established sign
template.
• The Town crew installs the sign and reports the completed installation back to the Town
Clerk.
• The Town Clerk confirms the completed installation with the Vilas County Clerk.
4. Sign Design Standards
All address/fire number signs shall conform to Vilas County General Code of Ordinances
Chapter 28, Appendix A, including the following:
• Signs shall be oriented horizontally and printed on both sides.
• Signs shall be installed perpendicular to the road.
• Signs shall use white block lettering/numbering, and shall include the name of the Town
(minimum 1 inch high) and the address number (minimum 3½ inches high). Road
names are optional.

Town of Winchester — Address/Fire Number Sign Policy
Policy 2026-04 — Page 3
• Sign background color shall be blue, green, or red, unless an alternate color is approved
by Vilas County.
• Signs shall be a minimum of 6 inches high and as wide as necessary to accommodate the
required information.
The Town of Winchester currently orders signs through Lange Signs. Clerks shall use the
established sign template for Winchester, which incorporates the Town name and conforms to
County design standards. See the final pages of this document for current design standards.
5. Placement Standards
All address/fire number signs shall be installed in conformance with Vilas County General
Code of Ordinances Chapter 28, Appendix A, including the following:
• Signs shall be securely fastened on U-channel metal posts. Alternate mounting methods
require prior County approval.
• Signs shall be placed on whichever side of the driveway best associates the sign with the
driveway or structure while ensuring maximum visibility.
• Signs shall be located within 20 feet of both the driveway and the road edge, and shall be
installed uniformly throughout the Town. Alternate locations require prior County
approval.
• Signs shall be installed approximately 4½ to 5 feet above road level.
6. Fees
6.1 Initial Installation (New Address)
A fee of $50.00 is assessed for the initial installation of an address/fire number sign for a new
address.

6.2 Replacement Signs
A replacement sign fee of $50.00 shall be assessed to the property owner when a sign requires
replacement due to damage, loss, theft, vandalism, or other cause attributable to the property
owner or a third party.
6.3 No-Fee Replacements
No fee shall be charged when a sign is replaced due to a readdressing situation initiated by
either the Town or Vilas County. The resident bears no cost for a sign replacement made
necessary by Town- or County-initiated readdressing.
Fee amounts may be amended from time to time by Town Board resolution without
amendment of this policy.

WHEREAS, the Town of Winchester is required to maintain accurate financial records and
prepare annual financial reports in accordance with Wis. Stat. §§ 60.40 and 66.0605, and
applicable Wisconsin Department of Revenue (DOR) reporting requirements; and
WHEREAS, the Wisconsin Department of Revenue has established a Uniform Chart of
Accounts for Wisconsin Municipalities, which provides a standardized system of account
codes and classifications for municipal revenues, expenditures, assets, liabilities, and fund
balances; and
WHEREAS, use of the Uniform Chart of Accounts promotes consistency, transparency, and
comparability in municipal financial reporting, facilitates preparation of the Annual Report of
Financial Transactions, and simplifies the Town’s accounting and audit processes; a nd
WHEREAS, the Town Board finds it in the best interest of the Town of Winchester and its
residents to formally adopt the Wisconsin DOR Uniform Chart of Accounts as the Town’s
official accounting classification system to ensure consistent, accurate, and auditable financial
records going forward.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Town Board of the Town of
Winchester, Vilas County, Wisconsin, as follows:

Response and turnout time
Turnout time, from dispatch until responding, was under 90 seconds 80% of the time.
August average turnout time is 1.2 minutes.
Average response time for the month of August was 10.98 minutes. This is from the time
of 911 call received to arrival at patient. Response times are obtained through Vilas
Dispatch Center.
Transport and Billing
28 of the 42 responses were transported. “Not Billed” responses included those that
refused transport following medical evaluation or no patient identified. Of the 28
responses that were transported, 20 responses benefited from Paramedic Level care
with four requiring significant intervention. Paramedic level care is defined as intervention
beyond IV placement. 583.2 loaded miles were recorded.
Crew / Organization Activities
NEMSD staff were able to provide support for a race and stand-by for a successful Musky
Jam in Boulder Junction. This is a great opportunity for residents and visitors to meet our
staff and ask questions about our operations. Also in August, we were provided our 2nd
quarter “report card” from the Coverdell Stroke Program. The data revealed that our staff
either met or exceeded every metric for managing patients with a possible stroke.

WHEREAS, the Town of Winchester is required to maintain accurate financial records and
prepare annual financial reports in accordance with Wis. Stat. §§ 60.40 and 66.0605, and
applicable Wisconsin Department of Revenue (DOR) reporting requirements; and
WHEREAS, the Wisconsin Department of Revenue has established a Uniform Chart of
Accounts for Wisconsin Municipalities, which provides a standardized system of account
codes and classifications for municipal revenues, expenditures, assets, liabilities, and fund
balances; and
WHEREAS, use of the Uniform Chart of Accounts promotes consistency, transparency, and
comparability in municipal financial reporting, facilitates preparation of the Annual Report of
Financial Transactions, and simplifies the Town’s accounting and audit processes; a nd
WHEREAS, the Town Board finds it in the best interest of the Town of Winchester and its
residents to formally adopt the Wisconsin DOR Uniform Chart of Accounts as the Town’s
official accounting classification system to ensure consistent, accurate, and auditable financial
records going forward.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Town Board of the Town of
Winchester, Vilas County, Wisconsin, as follows:

RESOLVED, that the Town Board of the Town of Winchester hereby formally adopts the

as the Town’s official system of account classifications for all municipal financial records,
effective upon adoption of this Resolution; and
FURTHER RESOLVED, that all Town officers, employees, and agents responsible for
financial recordkeeping shall classify revenues, expenditures, assets, liabilities, and fund
balances in accordance with the account codes and definitions set forth in the Wisconsin
DOR Uniform Chart of Accounts, as updated from time to time by the Wisconsin
Department of Revenue; and
FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Town Treasurer and Town Clerk are jointly directed to
ensure that the Town’s financial software, ledgers, and reporting systems are configured to
align with the Uniform Chart of Accounts, and to make any necessary adjustments to existing
account classifications to achieve compliance; and
FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Town Clerk shall file a certified copy of this Resolution
in the Town’s permanent records and shall maintain a current copy of the Wisconsin DOR
Uniform Chart of Accounts for reference by Town officers and staff.

General Records Schedule Policy
Upon Public Records Board (PRB) approval of a General Records Schedule (GRS), the implementation of said
schedules by Wisconsin state agencies is mandatory and immediate. Implementation of a PRB-commissioned
GRS by the UW System Administration, all UW campuses, all Wisconsin counties, municipalities or other local
units of government is optional but recommended. This policy is in accordance with the authority outlined
under Wis. Stats. § 16.61.
Policy Statement
General Record Schedules are a mechanism for systematic retention and disposition of similar types of records
across all government units. GRSs eliminate the need for state agencies to develop and seek approval of their
own records retention disposition authorizations (RDAs). They lend consistency to recordkeeping across all
government units and provide assurance of accountability to the public. The PRB supports the development of,
and has approved, GRSs in several functional areas. This policy statement mandates usage and implementation
of these schedules, as well as outlines a process and requirements that state agencies must use to opt out of any
or all of them, in whole or in part. See page 3 for implementation guidance and frequently asked questions. For
additional information on use of the GRS see the Introduction to General Records Schedules.
All state agencies are bound by this policy. State agencies may choose to opt out of a GRS, in whole or in part;
however, to opt out in whole or in part, an agency must develop corresponding RDAs of their own within 12
months from the date of the GRS approval, citing justification for the unique requirement. During that time, and
until their replacement, the agency will be bound by retention schedules which have been approved by the PRB
in the General Records Schedule.
UW System Administration, all UW campuses, all Wisconsin counties, municipalities or other local units of
government may:
Opt In: The UW System Administration, all UW campuses, all Wisconsin counties, municipalities or other
local units of government may opt in, using the Notification of General Schedule Adoption form (PRB-002),
and agree to use the recommendations noted in the GRS for its records. (State agencies do not have this
option because any GRS is mandatory and immediate on approval).
Opt In with Revisions: The UW System Administration, all UW campuses, all Wisconsin counties,
municipalities or other local units of government may opt in with revisions using the Notification of General
Schedule Adoption form (PRB-002). They agree to use some of the recommendations of the GRS and also
submit a list of records series they will be opting in to or out of. They must develop and submit to the PRB
corresponding records series of their own within 12 months from the date of GRS approval for any record
series they opt out of. It is recognized that local units may in some areas have the need to retain items for a
longer period of time than that recommended by the GRS. This is an internal business decision and can be
done without any action. (State agencies do not have this option because any GRS is mandatory and
immediate on approval).
State agencies, UW System Administration, all UW campuses, all Wisconsin counties, municipalities or other
local units of government may:
Opt Out: State agencies may opt out of a GRS in whole or in part, using the Notification of General Schedule
Adoption form (PRB-002). The agency must develop, and submit to the PRB, within 12 months, RDA(s) for

the records covered by the GRS which they chose to opt out of citing justification for the unique
requirement. Until they receive PRB approval for those RDAs, they will be bound by the GRS.
State agencies should be aware that current law (Wis. Stat. § 16.61) requires authorization of the PRB to destroy
any state agency records. Therefore, if a state agency chooses to opt out of any existing GRS, they may not
dispose of any records until the RDAs prepared by the state agency have been approved by the Public Records
Board and the retention period reached.
Wisconsin counties, municipalities and other local units of government should be aware of how current law
(Wis. Stat. § 19.21(4)(b) & (5)(c) respectively) addresses record retention and disposition, as well as PRB
authorization.
Revised November 2017
Implementing General Records Schedules
Upon PRB approval, agencies will use an identified GRS for any applicable records in its custody. This means that
following approval, records should continue to be disposed on a regular basis, provided that the minimum
retention time identified in the GRS has been met. Records must be retained for the minimum retention time
approved in the GRS and cannot be disposed of in a shorter amount of time. If a GRS identifies a record series
with a disposition of transfer to an archival repository, those records must be offered to the archival repository
rather than being destroyed. Destruction or transfer of records is contingent on record disposition restrictions
contained in Wis. Stat. § 19.35 (5) (Open Records Law). No records may be destroyed or transferred if litigation
or audit involving the records has commenced.
State agencies may discontinue the use of all, or portions of, any GRS, but the agency records officer must first
notify the PRB of the discontinuance, by following the steps noted in the policy above. When an agency
discontinues use of a GRS, the records controlled by the applicable record series may no longer be destroyed or
transferred until separate RDAs are prepared by the agency and approved by the PRB. Until that time, the
agency must continue to abide by the retention and disposition in the existing GRS.
General Records Schedule (GRS) -- Frequently Asked Questions
1. What happens to pre-existing General Records Schedules when an amended or renewed GRS is approved?
The pre-existing GRS is superseded by the new GRS immediately upon approval.
2. What happens when a General Records Schedule (GRS) automatically goes into effect?
Upon Public Records Board (PRB) approval of a General Records Schedule (GRS), the implementation of
said schedules by Wisconsin state agencies is mandatory and immediate.
3. What happens to any pre-existing agency Records Disposition Authorizations (RDAs) on topics covered by
a General Records Schedule (GRS)?
a. Pre-existing agency RDAs with a longer retention period stand until their sunset date is reached.
i. The agency Records Officer should submit the appropriate form to formally supersede the
pre-existing RDA before the sunset date is reached.
b. Pre-existing agency RDAs with a shorter retention period must be acted on within 12 months of the
GRS approval date. Until that time, the agency must abide by the GRS. Appropriate action includes:
superseding or amending.
i. The agency Records Officer should submit the appropriate form to supersede or amend the
pre-existing RDA.
c. Any pre-existing RDAs with a shorter retention period which the agency does not act on within 12
months, will become obsolete and
i. The longer GRS mandated retention time must be followed and
Revised November 2017
ii. The agency Records Officer must submit the appropriate form to formally close the pre-
existing RDA.
4. Why would an agency business unit choose to submit their own RDA for records covered by a GRS RDA?
a. Unique retention requirements for a set of specific business unit records. Requested retention
period cannot be shorter than the approved GRS retention.
b. Unique disposition requirements for a set of specific business unit records which is different than
the approved GRS.
Note: A state agency cannot dispose of records covered by the GRS until the business unit RDA is
approved by the PRB.
5. What happens when the entire agency opts out of a GRS in whole or in part?
State agencies may opt out of a GRS in whole or in part, using the Notification of General Schedule
Adoption form (PRB-002). The agency must develop and submit to the PRB, within 12-months, RDA(s)
for the records covered by the GRS which they chose to opt out of citing justification for the unique
requirement. Until they receive PRB approval for those RDAs, they will be bound by the GRS.
Appropriate justification includes: statute, code, or other legal authority.

Policy 2026-06 — Page 2
1. Purpose
This policy establishes the circumstances under which a facility use fee or security deposit paid
under the Town Facility Use Policy (Policy 2026-01) may be refunded, the process for
requesting and approving a refund, and how approved refunds are issued.
2. Refund Eligibility
A refund of the facility use fee, security deposit, or both may be issued only under one of the
following circumstances:
2.1 Timely Cancellation by the Applicant
Cancellations made at least 7 days prior to the scheduled use are eligible for a full refund of the
use fee and security deposit, consistent with the cancellation terms in Policy 2026-01 § 1.3.
2.2 Town-Initiated Cancellation
If the Town cancels a reservation for any reason — including but not limited to severe
weather, emergency use of the facility, staffing unavailability, or an inadvertent double-
booking — the applicant is eligible for a full refund of the use fee and security deposit,
regardless of how much advance notice was given.
2.3 Unsatisfactory Facility Condition
If the facility was unclean, damaged, or had non-functional equipment or utilities at the time
of use, the applicant may request a full or partial refund of the use fee. The request must
include supporting evidence (such as photographs, a written description of the issue, or
witness accounts) documenting the condition of the facility at the time of use.
3. Non-Qualifying Circumstances
Refunds are not available for cancellations made fewer than 7 days prior to the scheduled use,
except where Section 2.2 applies. In such cases, the use fee is forfeited and the security deposit
is returned, consistent with Policy 2026-01 § 1.3 and § 3.2.

4. Requesting a Refund
• Refund requests must be submitted in writing to the Town Clerk’s Office at
clerk@winchester.wi.gov or 715-686-2123 within 3 days after the scheduled reservation.
• Requests based on unsatisfactory facility condition (Section 2.3) must include
supporting evidence at the time the request is submitted.
• The applicant named on the original Facility Use Agreement must submit the request, or
provide written authorization for another party to do so on their behalf.
5. Approval Process
5.1 Routine Refunds
The Town Clerk is authorized to approve and process refund requests that clearly qualify
under Section 2.1 (timely cancellation) or Section 2.2 (Town-initiated cancellation) without
further Town Board action.
5.2 Exceptions & Disputes
Requests based on unsatisfactory facility condition (Section 2.3), requests that do not clearly
meet the criteria in Section 2, and any disputed refund amount shall be referred to the Town
Board for review and approval at a regular or special meeting.
6. Refund Method
• Approved refunds are issued by Town check or by digital reversal to the original online
payment method.
• No cash refunds are issued, regardless of the original payment method.
• Cash payments approved for refund are issued by Town check.

TOWN OF WINCHESTER, VILAS COUNTY, WISCONSIN
ORDINANCE NO. 2026-05
ALTERNATE CLAIMS APPROVAL PROCEDURE AND ELECTRONIC
APPROVAL OF CLAIMS; AMENDING ORDINANCE NO. 2020-02
SECTION I – PURPOSE
The purpose of this ordinance is to establish an alternate procedure, under Wis. Stat. §
60.44(2), for approving financial claims against the Town of Winchester which are in the
nature of bills and vouchers, so that routine claims may be reviewed and approved by the
Town Clerk between Town Board meetings, and to authorize that such written approval may
be documented electronically, including but not limited to email, Microsoft Teams messages
or an approved Teams-based approval workflow, or another Town Board–approved
electronic messaging or approval platform.
SECTION II – AUTHORITY
The Town of Winchester has the authority to enact this ordinance pursuant to the following:
A. Wis. Stat. § 60.44(2), authorizing the Town Board to provide, by ordinance, a procedure
for approving financial claims against the Town in the nature of bills and vouchers,
under which payment may be made after the Town Clerk reviews and approves in
writing each bill or voucher as a proper charge against the treasury; and Wis. Stat. §
66.0607(1) and (3), governing disbursement from the town treasury and the use of
facsimile signatures on drafts, orders, and checks.

B. Wis. Stat. §§ 137.15 and 137.25, governing the legal effect of electronic records and
electronic signatures, and the consent of a governmental unit to receive records and
signatures in electronic form. This ordinance also corrects the authority citation in
Ordinance No. 2020-02, which referenced “s. 66.0607(3) and 60.44(e), Wis. Stats.” —
the correct citations are Wis. Stat. §§ 66.0607(3) and 60.44(2).
SECTION III – RELATION TO ORDINANCE NO. 2020-02
Ordinance No. 2020-02 (Finance Ordinance), including its provisions on signature requirements for
drafts and checks, internal transfers, facsimile signatures, and electronic/ACH periodic payments,
remains in full force and effect. This ordinance supplements Ordinance No. 2020-02 by addressing when
and how the Town Clerk may approve a claim for payment, rather than who signs the resulting check.
A. Ordinance No. 2020-02, Section IV(1)–(4), continues to govern who signs Town drafts
and checks, including the use of facsimile signatures approved by the Town Board.
B. This ordinance governs the separate question of claims approval — i.e., when a bill or
voucher may be paid — and does not alter Ordinance No. 2020-02’s signature
requirements.
SECTION IV – ALTERNATE CLAIMS APPROVAL PROCEDURE
Claims in the nature of bills and vouchers against the Town of Winchester may be paid from the town
treasury, under Wis. Stat. § 66.0607, after the Town Clerk reviews and approves each bill or voucher in
writing as a proper charge against the treasury, without prior audit or approval of the individual claim
by the Town Board at a meeting, upon determining that funds are available under the town budget; the
item or service has been duly authorized; the item or service has been supplied or rendered in conformity
with the authorization; and the claim appears to be a valid claim against the Town.
A. The Town Clerk may require submission of proof to determine compliance with the
conditions above, including verification of quantity, quality, or delivery by another town
official or employee.

B. This section does not affect the applicability of Wis. Stat. § 893.80, and no action may be
brought or maintained against the Town upon a claim unless the claimant complies with
that section.
C. The Town Clerk shall document all claims approved under this procedure as follows:
1. The Town Clerk shall file with the Town Board, at least monthly, a list of the claims
approved under this procedure, showing the date paid, name of claimant, purpose,
and amount.
2. All claims and approvals shall be retained as part of the claim file, whether in paper or
electronic form.
3. The Town Clerk shall confirm that the Town’s public depository has specimen or
facsimile signatures on file consistent with Ordinance No. 2020-02 before honoring
checks issued under this procedure.
SECTION V – ELECTRONIC APPROVAL OF CLAIMS
Pursuant to Wis. Stat. § 137.25(1), the Town of Winchester, as a governmental unit, consents to receive
and rely upon electronic records and electronic signatures in connection with the claims approval
procedure established by Section IV of this ordinance.
A. The Town Clerk’s written approval of a claim required under Section IV of this
ordinance may be documented and satisfied by any of the following, each of which
constitutes “in writing” for purposes of Wis. Stat. § 60.44(2)(a): an email from the Town
Clerk (or, in the Clerk’s absence, the Deputy Town Clerk) approving the specific bill or
voucher; a message, approval, or recorded action taken through Microsoft Teams,
including a Teams-based approval workflow or extension approved by the Town Board;
an approval recorded within the Town’s accounting or claims-management software
(e.g., QuickBooks) identifying the approving official, the claim approved, and the date of
approval; or any other electronic messaging or approval platform subsequently approved
by resolution or ordinance of the Town Board.

B. An electronic approval under this section shall be attributable to the Town Clerk (or

legal effect as a personal signature on a bill or voucher. Nothing in this section requires
the Town Clerk to use an electronic method; a personal signature on a bill or voucher
continues to satisfy Section IV of this ordinance.
SECTION VI – RECORDS RETENTION
All claims, approvals, and supporting documentation — whether in paper or electronic form — shall be
retained in accordance with the Wisconsin Municipal General Records Schedule (WMRS) as adopted
by the Town.
A. An electronic record documenting approval under Section V shall be capable of
retention and reproduction by the Town at the time of approval, consistent with Wis.
Stat. § 137.16(1).
B. The Town Clerk shall ensure that records of electronic approvals remain accessible and
retrievable for as long as required under the WMRS, regardless of the platform used to
document the approval.
SECTION VII – SEVERABILITY
Should any section, clause, or provision of this ordinance be declared invalid by a court of
competent jurisdiction, such invalidity shall not affect the validity of the ordinance as a whole
or any part thereof other than the part so declared to be invalid.
SECTION VIII – NO ABROGATION OF ORDINANCE NO. 2020-02
This ordinance does not rescind, replace, or otherwise abrogate Ordinance No. 2020 -02.
Ordinance No. 2020-02 remains in full force and effect and is supplemented, not superseded,
by this ordinance.

and accepted at the Special Meeting on June 2, 2026.
Motion: To approve the minutes as amended.
Moved: Newton • Seconded: Silvis • Vote: Carried 2-0

TOWN OF WINCHESTER EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK
Effective 5/18/2023
Introduction and Purpose
Introductory Statement
This Employee Handbook is designed to acquaint employees with their Employer, the Town of
Winchester. It provides information about working conditions, employee benefits and policies affecting
employment. It also describes many employee responsibilities and gives the Town Board a means of
ensuring cooperative and harmonious working relationships.
No employee handbook can anticipate every circumstance or policy question. The Winchester Town
Board (Town Board) reserves the right to revise, supplement or rescind any policies or portion of the
Employee Handbook from time to time as deemed appropriate in its sole and absolute discretion.
Employees will be notified of changes to the Employee Handbook as they are made and will be required
to acknowledge receipt thereof.
The Town values constructive comments and suggestions from employees regarding work methods and
operations. Employees should feel free to offer suggestions and to seek advice on any work-related
matter of concern to them. The goals of the Town and its employees are best accomplished by mutual
effort and direct and honest communication.
This Employee Handbook is not a contract of employment and should not be construed as creating
a contract, expressed or implied, between the Town and any of its employees, nor is it a guarantee
of employment for any specific duration.
Purpose
The purpose of the Town of Winchester Employee Handbook is to provide a management framework,
benefits description and policy resource for all Town employees. Nothing in this handbook is intended
to create a legally binding contract or to change the at-will classification of employment with the Town
of Winchester. The Town of Winchester possesses management rights enabling it to exclusively manage
its operations in the best interest of Winchester citizens and taxpayers. The personnel policies contained
herein apply to all Town employees.
Employment with the Town of Winchester is an at-will relationship. Employees voluntarily enter into
employment with the Town of Winchester and are fee to resign at any time. Similarly, the Town of
Winchester may terminate the employment relationship at-will at any time provided applicable federal,
state or local laws have not been violated.
This Employee Handbook goes into effect beginning January 1, 2023. All previous policies or past
practices are hereby rescinded and superseded by this handbook. However, state and federal law take
precedence over this handbook in all cases.
2
Equal Opportunity
The Town of Winchester is an equal opportunity employer. In accordance with state law, the Town
encourages and fosters the employment of all persons regardless of their age, race, creed, color, sex,
sexual orientation, disability, national origin, ancestry, religious or political beliefs. The Town will
make a reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities.
Responsibility and Authority
The Winchester Town Board of Supervisors shall, as the appointing authority, have jurisdiction over
Town departments, committees, services, and employees, including but not limited to the following:
1. Allocating and establishing the number of positions required to efficiently operate each
department.
2. Filling of all vacancies.
3. Job descriptions.
4. Labor contracts.
5. Salaries and increases for all personnel.
6. Fringe benefits for all personnel.
7. Leaves of absence and extended time off.
8. Selection of new employees.
9. Adopt rules and regulations for the administration of the personnel system.
10. Discipline of employees.
11. Termination of employees.
12. Layoff procedures.
13. Reviewing and acting as the final authority in all personnel actions.
Work Guidelines
A. All Employees
1. Refusing to perform a duty assigned by the Town Board is a rule violation.
2. The Town Board will be responsible for the scheduling of work.
3. Only town employees or Town Board members are allowed to ride in town vehicles unless
otherwise approved by the Town Board.
4. Town vehicles or equipment will not be used for personal uses.
5. No excessive speed, carelessness, abuse, or personal retaliation are allowed with town vehicles or
equipment.
6. Use of intoxicants or illegal substances while on duty or reporting to work under the influence of
an intoxicant or illegal substance is prohibited and is grounds for immediate dismissal.
7. Use of foul language will not be tolerated.
8. Employee responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:
a) Sweeping and cleaning the facility floor as necessary.
b) Cleaning the bathroom and office.
c) Overall condition of the buildings.
d) Any activity deemed necessary by the Town Board.
9. All Town buildings, vehicles and equipment will be locked when not in use.
3
10. The Town Board will perform a written annual performance review of each employee during the
month of September.
B. Town Crew
1. Town Crew Employees may purchase supplies or equipment for the town for less than $1000.
Purchases over $1000 must be approved by the Town Board. Receipts for all purchases must be
signed by the purchaser and submitted to the Town Clerk weekly.
2. Town Board approval is required for any road work involving permits.
3. A normal work week will consist of 40 hours with an unpaid half-hour lunch.
a) May to October normal work hours will be Monday through Thursday 5:00 AM to 3:30 PM;
b) During the remaining months normal work hours will be 5:00 AM to 1:30 PM.
4. Employees will be allowed a fifteen-minute rest break in the morning and in the afternoon, which
is included in the normal workday hours.
5. If weather or other circumstances cause situations that require employee(s) to work other than the
normal work hours, the employee(s) shall report as needed.
6. Overtime is paid for all hours over 40 per workweek.
7. Overtime compensation is one and one-half times the employee hourly rate.
8. A town employee will be paid for a minimum of two hours, if requested to come in after the
normal workday or on Saturday or Sunday.
9. Saturdays and Sundays are considered premium days and will be paid at one and one-half times
the regular hourly rate when called in to work.
C. Transfer Site Attendant
1. The Town of Winchester will furnish the attendant with all needed materials and equipment for
the safe operation of the transfer site.
2. The disposal of the recyclables and trash will be at the discretion of the Winchester Town Board
with input from the attendant.
3. The attendant will ensure all trash, recyclables, bulk household items, electronics, scrap metal,
batteries, oils, etc., are properly disposed of or placed in their proper container. NO “repurposed”
items shall be accepted or left at the site.
4. The attendant will ensure that all persons using the Transfer Site are Winchester residents,
property owners, or renters in the Town of Winchester.
5. Additional responsibilities of the Transfer Site Attendant include, but are not limited to the
following:
a) Ensure compactor hopper areas, around, below, and on the sides are cleaned at a
minimum of every week. Clean all storage areas, dumpster areas, electronics areas, scrap
metal areas at a minimum of every week.
b) Collect and secure correct fees for disposal of scheduled items. Assist and oversee the
placement of bulk items, electronic devices, scrap metal and appliances.
c) Report any problems with the Transfer Site to the Town Board.
d) Have fuel tanks for snow thrower filled and ready for work by October 30. Removal of
snow at the apron of the building, around all sides of both compactor bins, around and on
top of the emergency dumpsters, around the bulk items bin, and the aprons near the scrap
metal bin.
6. The attendant will not accept assistance from any person other than an employee of the Town or
an elected Town Official.
4
7. The Transfer Site Attendant may purchase supplies for the Town for less than $50. Purchases
over $50 must be approved by the Town Board. Receipts for purchases must be signed by the
purchaser and submitted to the Town Clerk weekly.
8. Transfer site hours are as follows, and may be changed as deemed necessary by the Town Board:
a) Monday, Thursday, Saturday: 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM, Sunday: 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM; open
to the town.
b) Friday: 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM; closed to the town for cleaning/maintenance/and
organization.
9. The attendant’s paid straight time hours will be Monday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday: 8:30
AM to 4:00 PM, Sunday: 8:30 AM to 1:00 PM
10. The Transfer Site will be closed for the following holidays:
a) New Year’s Day
b) 4th of July
c) Thanksgiving Day
d) Christmas Day
11. It is the attendant’s responsibility to secure an approved replacement employee and notify the
Town Board liaison in the event the attendant cannot or is unable to work its assigned hours.
Compensation
A. Payroll Procedures
1. Pay Periods are bi-weekly, with work weeks beginning at 12:00 AM Monday and Ending at
11:59 PM Sunday.
2. Each employee is responsible for maintaining and signing their own timecard and daily log.
Completed timecards must be delivered to the Town Clerk by 10:00 AM on the Monday
following the end of the pay period for authorization by a Town Board member.
3. Payroll will be deposited electronically into the employee’s bank account no later than 3 banking
days after the end of the pay period.
4. Wisconsin Retirement System (WRS) – All employees are eligible to participate in the WRS
beginning January 1, 2024. Winchester will match the employee contribution of payroll wages to
your WRS retirement account, up to the maximum the rate determined by the WRS.
B. PTO
1. Holidays – paid time off
a) There are nine paid holidays per year consisting of New Year’s Day, Good Friday,
Memorial Day, Fourth of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, Thanksgiving Friday,
Christmas Eve and Christmas Day. Holiday pay will be for 8 hours at regular rate.
b) Any listed holidays worked will be paid at double the hourly rate.
2. Vacations – paid time off
a) Vacation will consist of one week (40 hours) pay for one to two years worked, two weeks
(80 hours) for three to seven years worked, three weeks (120 hours) for eight to fifteen
years worked, and one day for each year after to a maximum of 20 days (160).
b) Eligibility for vacation time shall begin 90 days after date of hire.
c) Scheduling of the vacation time will be at the discretion of the Town Board Supervisor in
charge of the employee.
d) Scheduling of vacation will be based on seniority.
e) Employees must give a two week notice of a request for vacation.
f) Unused vacation days will not accrue.
5
3. Sick and bereavement – paid time off
a) For employees hired after January 1, 2022 sick leave accumulates at one ½ day per pay
period. Sick leave may accumulate to 13 days. When an employee terminates their
employment with the town for whatever reason, retirement, resignation, or dismissal,
they will be eligible for up to 13 days of pay for sick time accumulated.
b) Sick leave may be used for when a family member is ill or up to three personal days per
year. Family member is defined as: a person living in the household, children,
stepchildren, parents of the employee or spouse and stepparents.
c) The employee shall contact the Supervisor in charge when they will be absent from work
due to illness.
C. Retirement
1. Town Crew employees with a hire date prior to January 1, 2022 and are not participating in any
other town sponsored benefit program are eligible for a plan where the Town of Winchester will
contribute up to 25% of the employee’s gross salary to the retirement plan.
2. For full time employees, averaging 30 hours a week or more, Winchester will reimburse the cost
of an “HSA -Eligible” health plan up to a maximum amount determined by the town board.
3. The employee will own and manage the plan and Winchester will reimburse the cost of plan
premiums up to a maximum amount determined by the town board for the individual and his
family as an addition to the paycheck. There are plans in our area managed by both Aspirus and
Marshfield Clinic.
4. Also, Winchester will make an annual contribution to the employee-managed Health Savings
Account (HSA) in an amount determined by the IRS annually.
5. The employee is responsible for purchasing the insurance, paying all premiums, paying tax on
the premium reimbursement added to the paycheck and setting up the HSA. Winchester has
established a relationship with Wisconsin Benefit Planning to help you find a qualifying plan and
establish the HSA. They can be reached in Minocqua at 866-521-3386.
D. Transfer Site Attendant
1. Holidays – paid time off (PTO)
a) When New Year’s Day, 4th of July, Thanksgiving, or Christmas Day fall on Monday,
Thursday, Saturday, or Sunday the Transfer Site attendant will be paid for that day at
regular rate.
b) The attendant will be paid at double the hourly rate for hours worked for the following
holidays: Memorial Day and Labor Day.
c) PTO will consist of 10 days (80 hours) after one year worked.
d) PTO hours do not accrue.
e) Scheduling of PTO will be at the discretion of the Town Board. A two week notice to the
Town Board is required to take PTO unless the PTO is used for legitimate, unexpected
illness or an emergency. Employees who miss more than three consecutive scheduled
workdays may be required to present a doctor’s release to the Town Board to return to
work.
f) A maximum of three days of paid bereavement leave may be taken for a death in the
employee’s immediate family.
EMPLOYEE GRIEV ANCE PROCEDURE
6
Purpose: This grievance procedure is adopted pursuant to s.66.0509(1m), Wis. Stat. and is intended
to provide a timely and orderly review of disputes regarding: a) employee terminations, b) employee
discipline, and c) workplace safety.
Employees of the Town of Winchester shall follow this procedure and the Winchester Town Board of
Supervisors shall act as the governing board.
Definitions for terms used in the document:
“Days”: means calendar days, excluding legal holidays as defined in s. 995.20, Wis. Stat.
“Discipline”: means any employment action that results in disciplinary suspension without
pay, disciplinary reduction in pay or other benefits, disciplinary demotions and terminations.
The term “discipline” does not include verbal notices or reminders, written reprimands,
performance evaluations, documentation of employee acts and/or omissions in an employment
file, non-disciplinary adjustments to compensation or benefits, actions taken to address job
performance such as establishment of a performance improvement plan or job targets; placing an
employee on paid leave pending an internal investigation; or other personnel actions taken by the
employer for non-disciplinary reasons.
“Hearing Officer”: means the impartial hearing officer required pursuant to s.66.0509(1m)(d)2,
Wis. Stat. The hearing officer selected by the Winchester Town Board is Attorney Greg Harrold.
“Termination”: means a discharge from employment for rule violations, poor performance,
acts detrimental to the employer or other acts of misconduct. The term “termination” does not
include: a voluntary quit, completion of seasonal employment, completion of temporary
assignment, completion of contract, layoff or failure to be recalled from layoff at the expiration
of the recall period, retirement, job abandonment (“no call, no show” or other failure to report to
work) or termination of employment due to medical condition, lack of qualification or license or
any other cessation of employment not involving involuntary termination.
“Workplace Safety”: means any alleged violation of any standard established under state law
or rule or federal law or regulation relating to workplace safety.
Process and Timelines:
1. The employee must file a written grievance with the Town Clerk within 10 (ten) days of receipt
of the termination, discipline or actual or reasonable knowledge of the alleged workplace safety
issue. So that an earnest effort can be made to resolve the matter informally, the grievant must
discuss the issue with his/her immediate supervisor prior to filing the written grievance.
However, in the case of termination, such a meeting is not required. Grievance forms may be
obtained from the Town Clerk. The Town Clerk shall inform the employee’s immediate
supervisor and the governing board chair about receipt of the written grievance as soon as
practicable.
7
2. The employee’s immediate supervisor will meet with the grievant within 10 (ten) days of receipt
of the written grievance. The supervisor will provide the grievant with a written response within
(10) days of the meeting. A copy of the supervisor’s response shall be filed in the Town Clerk’s
office. If no one has been designated as the employee’s immediate supervisor, the employee will
meet with the governing board chair who shall then provide the written response.
3. The employee may request an appeal to the hearing officer by filing a written request with the
Town Clerk within 10 (ten) days of receiving the written response. The Clerk shall notify the
governing board chair and employee’s supervisor about the filing of the request for a hearing as
soon as practicable. The Town will work with the hearing officer and grievant to schedule a
mutually agreeable hearing date.
4. The hearing officer shall provide the employee and employee’s supervisor with a written
decision no later than 30 (thirty) days after the hearing date. The hearing officer shall also
provide the Town Clerk with a copy of the decision for filing in the Town Clerk’s office.
5. The non-prevailing party may file a written request with the Town Clerk for an appeal to the
governing board within 10 (ten) days of receipt of the hearing officer’s decision. The Town
Clerk shall notify the governing board chair about the request as soon as possible. The
governing board shall decide the matter and issue a written decision within 45 (forty-five) days
of the filing of the appeal. The Town Board may sustain, deny or modify the recommendation of
the impartial hearing officer. The decision of the governing board shall be final and binding. A
copy of the governing board decision shall be provided to the employee and filed in the Town
Clerks office.
6. All timelines may be extended by mutual written agreement of the governing board and
employee. Without such agreement, a failure of the employee to adhere to any of the specified
timelines shall preclude any further consideration of the grievance.
7. If the last day on which an event is to occur is a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, the time limit
is extended to the next day which is not a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday. A grievance or
request for an appeal is considered timely if received by the Town Clerk during normal business
or if postmarked by 11:59 PM on the due date.
8. If the grievance is not answered within the time limits, at any stage, the employee may proceed
to the next available step within 7 (seven) days.
9. The grievant and governing board may mutually agree in writing to waive a step or multiple
steps in this procedure.
10. Granting the requested or agreed upon remedy resolves the grievance.
Grievance Requirements:
The written grievance must contain:
1. A statement of the pertinent facts surrounding the nature of the grievance;
2. The date the incident occurred or the date the alleged workplace safety concern was
8
discovered;
3. The steps taken to informally resolve the grievance, the individuals involved in the attempted
resolution and the results of such discussion;
4. The specific remedy requested; and
5. A description of the workplace safety rule alleged to have been violated, if applicable.
Supervisor’s Response:
The supervisor’s written response to the employee’s written grievance must contain:
1. A statement of the date meeting between the employee and supervisor was held; and
2. A decision as to whether the grievance is sustained or denied.
Procedure Before the Hearing Officer: The hearing officer shall define the issues, identifying areas of
agreement and identifying the issues in dispute and hear evidence and arguments. The hearing officer
will determine whether the governing board acted in an arbitrary and capricious manner. A decision will
not have been arbitrary or capricious if it was made in the best interest of the governing board. In all
cases, the grievant shall have the burden of proof to support the grievance. This process does not
involve a hearing before a court of law; thus, the rules of evidence will not be strictly followed.
However, no factual findings may be based solely on hearsay evidence.
The hearing officer may require the employee and governing board to submit materials related to the
grievance and witness lists in advance of the hearing in order to expedite the hearing. The hearing
officer shall sustain or deny the decision of the employee’s supervisor. The hearing officer is not given
authority to grant in whole or in part the specific request of the grievant. Within 30 (thirty) days after
the hearing, the hearing officer will issue a decision in writing indicating the findings and reasons for the
decision.
If the hearing officer’s decision on any grievance is appealed, only the issues raised in the hearing may
be appealed. Issues are not subject to modification in the appeal process.
Hearing Officer’s Decision:
The hearing officer’s written decision must contain:
1. A statement of pertinent facts surrounding the nature of the grievance;
2. A decision as to whether the grievance is sustained or denied, with the rationale for the
decision; and
3. A statement outlining the timeline to appeal the decision.
Representation: Both the employee and the governing body may be assisted by a representative of
their own choosing in person or by teleconference at any point during the grievance process.
Consolidation: The employee’s immediate supervisor and/or the hearing officer may consolidate
grievances where a reasonable basis for consolidation exists.
If more than one employee is grieving the same issue or circumstance, a single grievance form may be
used. A group grievance must be signed by all grieving employees and must indicate that it is a group
grievance at the first step in the grievance process.
9
Costs: Any expense incurred by an employee in investigating, preparing or presenting a grievance shall
be the sole responsibility of the employee. Each party (employee and employer) shall bear its own costs
for witnesses and all other out-of-pocket expenses, including possible attorney fees. The fees of the
impartial hearing officer shall be divided equally between the parties with the employee(s) paying half
and the employer paying the other half.

General Records Schedule
Facilities Management and Related Records
Approved by the Public Records Board:
November 18, 2019
Revised: June 13, 2022
Expiration: November 18, 2029
For use by all units of Wisconsin Government at the State, County, and Municipal level
1 | P a g e
I. Scope
This schedule governs the records retention obligations of state agencies pursuant to Wis. Stat. § 16.61, and applies to “public records”
as defined in Wis. Stat. § 16.61(2)(b). These “public records” are referred to as “records” in this schedule.
This schedule covers records which most state agencies, including the University of Wisconsin System Administration, the University of
Wisconsin Institutions, all Wisconsin counties, municipalities and other units of local government create and use to administer facilities
related records. The schedule is applicable to facilities related records regardless of format or media.
This general schedule may not include records which are unique to the mission of a single government unit. Records that are unique to
the mission of a specific government unit require a separate Records Disposition Authorization (RDA). The department or institution is
responsible for creating a RDA that must be submitted to, and approved by, the Public Records Board (PRB).
See the Introduction to General Records Schedules for additional information about how to use this schedule. In particular please
review the restrictions on conditions that might preclude the authorized destruction of documents in the normal course of business
including open records requests, ongoing legal holds, or audits currently underway or known to be planned.
This schedule goes into effect upon final approval by the Public Records Board.
II. Records Format
Records covered in this schedule may be in paper, electronic, or other formats. Electronic format examples include those created or
transmitted via e-mail, data contained in database systems, and tapes/cartridges. To safeguard the information contained in records
maintained exclusively in electronic format, agencies must meet the standards and requirements for the management of electronic
records outlined in Wis. Admin. Code ch. Admin 12.
As of October 1, 2015, most state agencies are using STAR (PeopleSoft) as the infrastructure for finance, budget, procurement,
business intelligence and human resource functions.
The Facilities Management Information Center (FMIC) provides centralized support for Facilities Management functions. The FMIC
provides a central clearinghouse for obtaining information for over 30 state facilities managed by the Department of Administration.
WisBuild is an online project management tool which is available to staff, architects, engineers, and contractors working on state
building projects. A/E firms and contractors must register to gain Wisbuild access.
2 | P a g e
III. Personally Identifiable Information
Wisconsin law requires authorities to specifically identify certain record series within a general records schedule that contain Personally
Identifiable Information (PII). Wisconsin Stat. § 19.62(5) defines PII broadly as “information that can be associated with a particular
individual through one or more identifiers or other information or circumstances.” Despite this broad definition, Wis. Stat. §
16.61(3)(u)(2) , requires that record series within a schedule containing the following types of PII need not be identified as such: a) the
results of certain computer matching programs; b) mailing lists; c) telephone or e-mail directories; d) record series pertaining exclusively
to agency employees; and e) record series that contains PII incidental to the primary purpose for which the records series was created,
and f) those relating to state agency procurement or budgeting. If in doubt as to whether a specific record series contains PII, check
with your agency legal counsel.
IV. Confidentiality of Records
Most records are not confidential and are open to public disclosure, however, there are exceptions. This GRS will identify any record
series that may contain information required by law to be kept confidential or specifically required to be protected from public access,
identifying the state or federal statute, administrative rule, or other legal authority that so requires. If in doubt as to whether or not a
specific record, or content in that record, is confidential, check with your agency legal counsel. A record series should be identified as
confidential even if not all records in the series contain confidential information and not all parts of records covered by the series are
confidential.
V. Superseded Record Series
“Superseded” means that a new record series or RDA number has been used to cover records that were previously identified
differently. The last column in the following GRS table titled “Previous RDA Number (if applicable)” provides a cross walk between new
and any superseded RDA numbers. When revising a GRS, an attempt is made to retain the previous RDA number, providing the
underlying records remain the same.
VI. Related Records
The “Related Records Series” section provides information on other record series in approved GRSs which may relate to the broader
functional area of this GRS. These record series are listed to facilitate a more complete understanding of all the record series within the
broad scope of this function of government. It may not however contain a complete listing of all records series used within your agency
for these types of business records. See the “Related Records Series” section included in this document.
3 | P a g e
VII. Closed Record Series
When revising a GRS it is common for some previously included record series to be closed. The “Closed Series” section lists series
containing records that are no longer created, nor are they expected to be in the future. See the “Closed Series” section included in this
document.
VIII. Revision History
See the “Revision History” section for a listing of changes to this GRS.

General Records Schedule
Human Resources and Related Records
Approved by the Public Records Board:
March 25, 2019
Revised: November 21, 2022
Expiration: March 25, 2029
For use by all units of Wisconsin Government at the State, County, and Municipal level
1 | P a g e
I. Scope
This schedule governs the records retention obligations of state agencies pursuant to Wis. Stat. § 16.61, and applies to “public records”
as defined in Wis. Stat. § 16.61(2)(b). These “public records” are referred to as “records” in this schedule.
This schedule covers records which most state agencies, the University of Wisconsin System Administration, the University of
Wisconsin Institutions, all Wisconsin counties, municipalities and other units of local government create and use to administer Human
Resources records. The schedule is applicable to human resources records regardless of format or media. For further information on
policies and procedures, refer to the Wisconsin Human Resources Handbook.
See the Introduction to General Records Schedules for additional information about how to use this schedule and for further information
on who may use General Records Schedules. In particular, please review the restrictions on conditions that might preclude the
authorized destruction of documents in the normal course of business including open records requests, ongoing legal holds, or audits
currently underway or known to be planned.
The broad categories within the document are:
• General Policies and Procedures
• Recruitment and Selection
• Classification and Compensation
• Workforce Management
• Employment Relations
• Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity
• Medical
• Employee Assistance (EAP)
• Training
• General Human Resource Administration
This general schedule may not include records which are unique to the mission of a single government unit. Records that are unique to
the mission of a specific government unit require a separate Records Disposition Authorization (RDA). The department or institution is
responsible for creating an RDA that must be submitted to, and approved by, the Public Records Board (PRB).
This schedule goes into effect upon final approval by the Public Records Board.
2 | P a g e
II. Records Format
Records covered in this schedule may be in paper, electronic, or other formats. Electronic format examples include those created or
transmitted via e-mail, data contained in database systems, and tapes/cartridges. To safeguard the information contained in records
maintained exclusively in electronic format, agencies must meet the standards and requirements for the management of electronic
records outlined in Wis. Admin. Code ch. Admin 12.
As of October 1, 2015, most state agencies are using STAR (PeopleSoft) as the infrastructure for finance, budget, procurement,
business intelligence, and human resource functions. Most human resources functions began utilizing STAR in December 2015.
III. Personally Identifiable Information
Wisconsin law requires authorities to specifically identify certain record series within a general records schedule that contain Personally
Identifiable Information (PII). Wisconsin Stat. § 19.62(5) defines PII broadly as “information that can be associated with a particular
individual through one or more identifiers or other information or circumstances.” Despite this broad definition, Wis. Stat. §
16.61(3)(u)(2) , requires that record series within a schedule containing the following types of PII need not be identified as such: a) the
results of certain computer matching programs; b) mailing lists; c) telephone or e-mail directories; d) record series pertaining exclusively
to agency employees; and e) record series that contains PII incidental to the primary purpose for which the records series was created,
and f) those relating to state agency procurement or budgeting. If in doubt as to whether a specific record series contains PII, check
with your agency legal counsel.
Information about identity theft and information security is available at http://itsecurity.wi.gov/.
IV. Confidentiality of Records
Most records are not confidential and are open to public disclosure; however, there are exceptions. This GRS will identify any record
series that may contain information required by law to be kept confidential or specifically required to be protected from public access,
identifying the state or federal statute, administrative rule, or other legal authority that so requires. If in doubt as to whether or not a
specific record, or content in that record, is confidential, check with your agency legal counsel. A record series should be identified as
confidential even if not all records in the series contain confidential information and not all parts of records covered by the series are
confidential.
3 | P a g e
V. Superseded Record Series
“Superseded” means that a new record series or RDA number has been used to cover records that were previously identified
differently. The last column in the following GRS table titled “Previous RDA Number (if applicable)” provides a cross walk between new
and any superseded RDA numbers. When revising a GRS, an attempt is made to retain the previous RDA number, providing the
underlying records remain the same.
VI. Related Records
The “Related Records Series” section provides information on other record series in approved GRSs which may relate to the broader
functional area of this GRS. These record series are listed to facilitate a more complete understanding of all the record series within the
broad scope of this function of government. It may not, however, contain a complete listing of all records series used within your agency
for these types of business records. See the “Related Records Series” section included in this document.
VII. Closed Record Series
When revising a GRS, it is common for some previously included record series to be closed. The “Closed Series” section lists series
containing records that are no longer created, nor are they expected to be in the future. See the “Closed Series” section included in this
document.
VIII. Revision History
See the “Revision History” section for a listing of changes to this GRS.

General Records Schedule
Risk Management and Related Records
Approved by the Public Records Board:
November 20, 2023
Expiration: November 20, 2033
For use by all units of Wisconsin Government at the State, County, and Municipal level
2 | P a g e
I. Scope
This schedule governs the records retention obligations of state agencies pursuant to Wis. Stat. § 16.61, and applies to “public
records” as defined in Wis. Stat. § 16.61(2)(b). These “public records” are referred to as “records” in this schedule.
This General Records Schedule (GRS) covers records which most state agencies, including the University of Wisconsin
System Administration, the University of Wisconsin Institutions, all Wisconsin counties, municipalities and other units of local
government create and use to administer risk management related records Pursuant to the GRS Policy, the implementation of
said schedules by Wisconsin state agencies is mandatory and immediate. Implementation of a GRS by the UW System
Administration, all UW campuses, all Wisconsin counties, municipalities or other local units of government is optional but
recommended. Adopting the schedule does not require local units to begin creating any record series that they currently do not
produce.
Wis. Stats. § 16.865 mandates responsibility for statewide risk management coordination. Pursuant to Wis. Stats. §16.865(5),
the Department of Administration (DOA) Bureau of State Risk Management (BSRM) is responsible to arrange appropriate
insurance contracts for the transfer of risk of loss on the part of the state or its employees to the extent such loss cannot
reasonably be assumed by individual agencies or self-funded programs. This includes providing insurance coverage for state
agencies. Agencies that receive authorization from the DOA’s BSRM may secure coverage for specific business purposes on
their own. Annually, the Bureau of State Risk Management under authority of Wis. Stat. §§ 16.865, and 20.865(1)(f), develops
fiscal year premium documents which support the State Risk Management Program or similar process within a government
unit.
This general schedule may not include records which are unique to the mission of a single government unit. Records that are
unique to the mission of a specific government unit require a separate Records Disposition Authorization (RDA). The
government unit is responsible for creating a RDA(s) that must be submitted to, and approved by, the Public Records Board
(PRB).
This schedule goes into effect upon final approval by the Public Records Board.
II. Introduction to General Records Schedules
See the Introduction to General Records Schedules for additional information about how to use this schedule. In particular,
please review the restrictions on conditions that might preclude the authorized destruction of documents in the normal course of
business including open records requests, ongoing legal holds, or audits currently underway or known to be planned. Also
included in the Introduction to GRSs you will find further information on: Who May Use GRSs, Records Responsibilities,
Records Format, Retaining Records, Confidential and Personally Identifiable Information, and Understanding the GRS
Categories. You should review this document before implementing a GRS.
