66.0113 Citations for certain ordinance violations.
(1) ADOPTION; CONTENT. (a) Except as provided in sub. (5), the
governing body of a county, town, city, village, town sanitary dis-
trict or public inland lake protection and rehabilitation district
may by ordinance adopt and authorize the use of a citation under
this section to be issued for violations of ordinances, including or-
dinances for which a statutory counterpart exists.
(b) An ordinance adopted under par. (a) shall prescribe the
form of the citation which shall provide for the following:
1. The name and address of the alleged violator.
2. The factual allegations describing the alleged violation.
3. The time and place of the offense.
4. The section of the ordinance violated.
5. A designation of the offense in a manner that can be read-
ily understood by a person making a reasonable effort to do so.
6. The time at which the alleged violator may appear in court
and a statement describing whether the appearance is mandatory.
7. A statement which in essence informs the alleged violator:
a. That the alleged violator may make a cash deposit of a
specified amount to be mailed to a specified official within a
specified time.
b. That if the alleged violator makes such a deposit, he or she
need not appear in court unless appearance is mandated by the
court or he or she is subsequently summoned.
c. That, if the alleged violator makes a cash deposit and does
not appear in court, he or she either will be deemed to have ten-
dered a plea of no contest and submitted to a forfeiture, plus
costs, fees, and surcharges imposed under ch. 814, not to exceed
the amount of the deposit or will be summoned into court to an-
swer the complaint if the court does not accept the plea of no
contest.
d. That, if the alleged violator does not make a cash deposit
and does not appear in court at the time specified, the court may
issue a summons or a warrant for the defendant’s arrest or con-
sider the nonappearance to be a plea of no contest and enter judg-
ment under sub. (3) (d), or the municipality may commence an
action against the alleged violator to collect the forfeiture, plus
costs, fees, and surcharges imposed under ch. 814.
e. That if the court finds that the violation involves an ordi-
nance that prohibits conduct that is the same as or similar to con-
duct prohibited by state statute punishable by fine or imprison-
ment or both, and that the violation resulted in damage to the
property of or physical injury to a person other than the alleged
violator, the court may summon the alleged violator into court to
determine if restitution shall be ordered under s. 800.093.
8. A direction that if the alleged violator elects to make a
cash deposit, the alleged violator shall sign an appropriate state-
ment which accompanies the citation to indicate that he or she
read the statement required under subd. 7. and shall send the
signed statement with the cash deposit.
9. Such other information as may be deemed necessary.
(c) An ordinance adopted under par. (a) shall contain a sched-
ule of cash deposits that are to be required for the various ordi-
nance violations, plus costs, fees, and surcharges imposed under
ch. 814, for which a citation may be issued. The ordinance shall
also specify the court, clerk of court, or other official to whom
cash deposits are to be made and shall require that receipts be
given for cash deposits.
(2) ISSUANCE; FILING. (a) Citations authorized under this
section may be issued by law enforcement officers of the county,
town, city, village, town sanitary district or public inland lake
protection and rehabilitation district. In addition, the governing
body of a county, town, city, village, town sanitary district or pub-
lic inland lake protection and rehabilitation district may designate
by ordinance or resolution other county, town, city, village, town
sanitary district or public inland lake protection and rehabilita-
tion district officials who may issue citations with respect to ordi-
nances which are directly related to the official responsibilities of
the officials. Officials granted the authority to issue citations
may delegate, with the approval of the governing body, the au-
thority to employees. Authority delegated to an official or em-
ployee shall be revoked in the same manner by which it is
conferred.
(b) The issuance of a citation by a person authorized to do so
under par. (a) shall be deemed adequate process to give the appro-
priate court jurisdiction over the subject matter of the offense for
the purpose of receiving cash deposits, if directed to do so, and

1. Reservations
1.1 Who May Reserve
• The applicant must be at least 18 years old.
• Reservations are open to residents, non-residents, and taxpayers of the Town of
Winchester. Reservations may be made on behalf of organizations.
• Residents, taxpayers, and local organizations have priority over non-residents on a first-
come, first-served basis.
1.2 How to Reserve
• Submit reservations in writing using the Town of Winchester Facility Use Request
Form. For assistance, contact the Clerk’s Office at clerk@winchester.wi.gov or 715 -686-
2123.
• Schedule with the Clerk’s Office at least one week and up to one year in advance of the
requested use date.
• A date is reserved only after the Clerk’s Office receives the completed request form, any
required payment, and confirms the reservation in writing.
• Fees and deposits may be paid via cash, check, or online payment system through the
town website (winchesterwi.com). Online payments may incur a service fee.
1.3 Cancellation Policy
• Cancellations made at least 7 days prior to the scheduled use will receive a full refund of
fees and deposits.
• Cancellations made fewer than 7 days prior to the scheduled use will result in forfeiture
of the $50 use fee. Deposits will be returned.
• To cancel, contact the Clerk at clerk@winchester.wi.gov or 715-686-2123.

2. User Responsibilities
2.1 General
• The applicant named on the Use Agreement must be present and is responsible for the
conduct of the event and all attendees.
• Use of Town of Winchester facilities is voluntary and is undertaken at the sole risk of the
facility user and/or the organization. The Town of Winchester is not responsible for
injuries, damages, or claims arising from the actions, omissions, or misuse of the facilities
by the facility user, the organization, or any participants or guests.
• To the fullest extent permitted by law, use of Town of Winchester facilities constitutes a
release of the Town of Winchester and its officers, employees, and agents from claims
related to such use. The facility user is responsible for defending and indemnifying the
Town against claims, damages, losses, or expenses arising from the use of the facilities or
from the actions of participants or guests.
• The facility user is responsible for reimbursing the Town for any damage, breakage,
repairs, extra cleaning, or other costs resulting from facility use.
• The applicant is responsible for complying with all state and local laws and agrees to hold
the Town of Winchester harmless for violations arising from the event.
• Violations may result in a cleaning fee and/or loss of facility-use privileges, at the
discretion of the Town Board.
2.2 Facility Care
• All lights must be turned off and all doors locked when leaving the building.
• Furniture and equipment must remain in the building.
• All chairs are to be returned to the storage area.
• Users are responsible for setting up and taking down tables. For safety reasons, the Town
recommends that at least two people perform this task.
• Tables should be wiped clean.
• Bathrooms must be left clean. Damage and cleaning assessed will be repaired at the
applicant’s expense.
• All garbage (inside and outside) must be bagged and removed by the applicant. Garbage
may be disposed of at the Winchester Transfer Station during its regular business hours.

and the applicant will be billed at the rate of $50 per hour.
• Do not use tacks, nails, staples, or tape for decorations.
• No fireworks.
• No animals, except dogs on a leash at outdoor facilities.
• Fire exits must remain unblocked at all times.
• Replacement or repair of missing or damaged items may be billed to the applicant.

• Wash, dry, and return pots, pans, and utensils to proper storage areas.
• Wipe sink and countertops.
• Unplug all coffee machines, crock pots, and similar appliances (except microwaves).

pursuant to Wis. Stat. § 125.51 and Town of Winchester Ordinance 2022-02 (Operator’s

• A Town of Winchester Class B license is required. — Wis. Stat. § 125.51
• Apply with the Town Clerk at least one week before a monthly Town Board meeting.

• A bartender licensed by the Town of Winchester must be present at all times during
service. — Town Ordinance 2022-02
• Minors are not allowed to be present where such beverages are sold unless accompanied
by a parent or legal guardian.
• The licensed applicant is responsible for compliance with all applicable laws, including
prohibition of sale to minors.
• Proof of liability insurance is required prior to issuance of the license.
• The licensed applicant will be held responsible for any violations of state or local law
related to the service of alcohol at the event.

INTERMUNICIPAL AGREEMET / BYLAWS
OF THE
NORTHWOODS EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES DISTRICT (NEMSD)
(
Approved Version, 10-30-24)
I. CREATION
1. CRE
ATION. Pursuant to Wis. Stat. § 66.0301(2) (Intermunicipal Agreement), and effective
March 1, 2024, there is hereby created the Northwoods Emergency Medical Services District
(NEMSD).
2. MEMBERS. The Members of the NEMSD include the following Entities:
A. Th
e Town of Boulder Junction
B. The Town of Manitowish Waters
C. The Town of Presque Isle
D. The Town of Winchester
II. AUT HORITY AND PURPOSE
1. AUT
HORITY AND PURPOSE. By virtue of the authority granted by W is. Stat. §§
60.23(1), 61.34(1), 61.64, and 66.0301, the Parties enter into this Agreement to create the
District to provide emergency medical services (EMS) within the District Territory.
Original: 2-15-24
Revised: 10-30-24
III. EMS DISTRICT CREATION AND POWERS
1. CREATION AND POWERS. The District is hereby created to provide
emergency medical services (EMS) in the District Territory. The District shall have
the following powers:
A. Operate an emergency medical service (EMS) department;
B. Own property;
C. Enter contracts;
D. Appoint a Chief / Service director of the department;
E. Hire and discharge District employees;
F. Retain consultants;
G. Prepare and approve annual operating and capital budgets;
H. Allocate among the Parties their proportionate share of the costs for
the maintenance and operation of the District, including future capital
improvements and equipment purchases, in accordance with this
Agreement.
I. Deposit and disburse funds to effectuate the purposes of this
Agreement;
B. Establish reasonable user charges for the provision of emergency medical services;
C. Adopt rules and regulations for the management and control of the District,
provided the rules and regulations are not inconsistent with Wisconsin law or this
Agreement;
D. Adopt rules and regulations for the conduct of its meetings, provided the rules and
regulations are consistent with Wisconsin law and this Agreement;
Original: 2-15-24
Revised: 10-30-24
E. Adopt policies allowing separate accounts for emergency medical technician
volunteer funds pursuant to Wis. Stat. § 66.0608.
F. Enter into intergovernmental cooperative agreements with other emergency medical
service districts, or any other municipality, town or county for the receipt,
furnishing or the cooperative employment of such services.
IV. AMBULANCE DISTRICT BOARD OF DIRECTORS
1. COMPOSITION. The NEMSD Board shall consist of four (4) voting Directors. One
Director shall be appointed by each of the Town Members (4 Directors total). The vote of each
voting Director shall be counted as one (1) vote.
2. APPOINTMENT. Town Members shall make appointments to the Board of Directors in
writing, received by the District Board prior to the first day of January of the year in which the
Board Director’s term begins. The Director serves at the will of the appointing Town Member,
and may be replaced by the Town Member. Alternate Directors may also be appointed by the
respective Town Member, who may vote in the absence of the Director.
3. TERM. In order to stagger terms, the length of term for the initial appointees shall be
determined by drawing numbers. Two Directors shall be for a one-year term; two Directors shall
be for a two-year term. After the initial term, the subsequent term for each appointed Director
shall be two years. The term of office shall begin at the first meeting of the Director in January.
A Director may serve up to a total of eight consecutive years.
4. VACANCIES. Upon the expiration of the term of a Director, the appointing Town Member
shall have the right to designate a successor as Director, or reappoint the current Director.
Original: 2-15-24
Revised: 10-30-24
5. VACANCIES PRIOR TO EXPIRATION OF TERM. In the event of the death,
resignation, or removal of a Director, the successor to such Director shall be selected by the
Town Member entitled to designate and appoint that representative to fill the unexpired term of
the Director. Three consecutive unexcused absences from scheduled District Board meetings
shall constitute a vacancy under this section.
V. OFFICERS
1. ELEC
TIONS. The District Board shall organize and elect from the Board a President, and a
Vice President. The Board shall also elect a Secretary and a Treasurer. The Secretary and the
Treasurer may be--but need not be--a District Board Director. Officers shall hold office for a
one-year term. New elections shall be held annually at the January District Board meeting.
2. RESIGNATION AND REMOVAL. Any officer may be removed from office with cause by
the District Board. Any officer may resign at any time by giving written notice to the District
Board. Such resignation shall take effect at the first Board meeting following receipt of such
notice. Any vacancy in Office may be filled by appointment by the Board. The officer
appointed shall serve for the remainder of the term of the officer replaced.
3. DUTIES. The duties of the Officers are as follows:
(a) President. The President shall:
~preside at all meetings of the Board;
~see that the orders and resolutions of the Board are carried out;
~sign all leases, mortgages, deeds, promissory notes and other written
instruments, as approved by the Board;
~review and approve all checks and payments.
Original: 2-15-24
Revised: 10-30-24
(b) Vice President. The Vice President shall act in the place and stead of the President in
the event of his or her absence, inability or refusal to act, and shall exercise and perform
such other duties as may be directed by the Board.
(c) Secretary. The Secretary shall:
~oversee the recording of Board votes;
~keep minutes for all meetings and proceedings of the Board;
~verify that Board meeting notices are served;
~ perform such other duties as may be directed by the Board.
(d) Treasurer. The Treasurer shall:
~oversee collection and investment of District Service funds;
~prepare reports and accountings with the assistance of EMS management;
~monitor compliance with year-to-date budget requirements;
~perform such other duties as may be directed by the Board.
VI. POWERS AND DUTIES OF THE BOARD
1. LIMITATION. The powers of the Board are limited to those powers expressly granted by
these Bylaws.
2. BYLAWS. The Board shall carry out the provisions of these Bylaws. Consistent with the
provisions of these Bylaws, the Board shall adopt such rules and regulations as are necessary to
carry out its responsibilities.
3. EQUIPMENT. The Board shall be responsible for the expenses related to the maintenance,
replacement, and upgrading of all EMS-related equipment owned or leased by the District.
Original: 2-15-24
Revised: 10-30-24
4. RECORDS. The Board shall see to it that complete and accurate records are kept and
maintained of all income and expenditures arising from the operation of the NEMSD, to see to
an annual audit of the service accounts by hiring a reputable certified public accounting firm
experienced in conducting municipal audits, and to prepare an annual report of District
operations for the annual meeting.
5. FEES. The Board shall set the Billing fees for the District Ambulance Service.
6. BUDGET. The Board shall adopt a budget prior to October 1st of each year showing
estimated income and expenditures of the service and setting proposed assessments for
ratification by the participating Towns.
7. SALARIES. The Board shall approve NEMSD personnel salaries, hourly wage rates, or any
other employee benefits.
8. CONTRACTS. The Board shall prepare any necessary contracts for communities
participating in the District Ambulance Service and enter into such other contracts as are
necessary to carry out Board duties and responsibilities.
9. LEGAL COUNSEL. The Board may retain legal counsel to advise the Board on all matters
concerning the Board and the operation of the NEMSD.
10. INSURANCE. The Board shall assure that adequate liability, worker’s compensation,
hazard, and property insurance are on all property, vehicles, and equipment owned or leased by
the NEMSD.
11. COMMITTEES/SUB-COMMITTEES. The Board may create Committees/Sub-
committees to work on assigned tasks and projects as needed. Each Committee/Sub-committee
shall be chaired by a Board Director. Others that may be appointed to the Committee/Sub-
Original: 2-15-24
Revised: 10-30-24
committee may include other Board Directors, Members of the Community, and Subject-matter
Experts.
VII. MEETINGS OF THE BOARD
1. REGULAR MEETINGS. The Board shall meet at least quarterly for the transaction of its
normal business.
2. SPECIAL MEETINGS. Special meetings of the Board may be called at any time by the
President or by a majority vote of the Board.
3. QUORUM. A majority of the voting Directors then serving shall constitute a quorum,
whether in person, or via Zoom or other electronic means.
4. VOTES OF THE BOARD. The vote of each Director shall be counted as one vote, for a
total of four (4) votes. If a quorum of Directors is present, then a majority of the votes
represented at the meeting, counted as provided in this paragraph, shall be the act of the Board.
VIII. EXPENDITURES AND BUDGET
1. PREPARATION. Prior to the first day of October of each year the Board shall submit to all
Members a proposed budget for the following year. Such budget shall include an estimate of
income and expenses for the NEMSD operations necessary for the ensuing year. The projected
expenses shall then be deducted from the projected income, to determine the minimum projected
deficit amount that shall be assessed to all Town Members.
2. ASSESSMENTS. Each Town Member shall be responsible for a proportionate share of the
ratified budget amount based upon the equalized value of each Town Member. Each Town
Member shall pay its proportionate share of the ratified District budget, in two equal payments.

31st of each year.
IX. ASSETS AND LIABILITIES
1. OWNERSHIP. All equipment, vehicles, and other property acquired or purchased by the
District shall be the property of the NEMSD. Ownership of all such property shall be titled in
the name of the NEMSD.
2. CONTROL OF PROPERTY. The Board shall have exclusive charge and custody of all
property and equipment owned or leased by it.

the Board Treasurer appointed under section III.3.(d).
4. EXPENDITURES. The Board shall have exclusive charge and control of the expenditure of
any monies appropriated to the NEMSD.
X. NEW MEMBERS
1. ADMISSION. The District Board by unanimous vote may admit new Members to the
NEMSD. Such new Members are subject to all rules, regulations and Bylaws of the NEMSD.
2. PURCHASE REQUIREMENTS. Each new Member shall be liable for the purchase of an
ownership share of the NEMSD assets. Assets shall be valued by the Board at their fair market
value as of the date of new Member entry. The District Board, in its discretion, may defer
payment of such amounts upon such terms and conditions as may be approved by the Board.

the end of any calendar year by giving written notice to the Secretary of the Board one year prior
to such termination. The Town Member shall remain liable for its assessed share of operating
costs for the remainder of that year, but not thereafter.

budget on or before the due date of any year shall be in default. Unless the default is cured by
full payment of all amounts due within 30 days of mailing of notice thereof to the defaulting

event of termination of Service, the defaulting Town Member shall remain liable for its assessed
share of operating costs for the entire year of termination together with interest at the annual rate
of 12% until paid.

1. CONTRACTS FOR SERVICE. The District Board by unanimous vote may approve
contracts for service with non-Member municipalities or other non-participating groups. Such

ownership interest in any assets of the Service, would have no voting rights at Annual Meetings,
and would not be entitled to representation on the District Board. No contract for service may be
entered into, if it would impair the ability of the NEMSD to provide ambulance service to the
Town Members.

INTERMUNICIPAL AGREEMENT
NORTHWOOD EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICE DISTRICT (NEMSD)
1. CREATION. Pursuant to Wis. Stat. § 66.0301(2) (Intermunicipal Agreement), and effective
May 15th, 2026, there is hereby created the Northwoods Emergency Medical Services District
(NEMSD).
2. MEMBERS. The Members of the NEMSD include the following municipalities hereinafter
referred to as Members.
A. The Town of Boulder Junction
B. The Town of Manitowish Waters
C. The Town of Presque Isle
D. The Town of Winchester
II. EMS DISTRICT AUTHORITY AND PURPOSE
1. By virtue of the authority granted by Wis. Stat. 60.23(1), 61.34(1), 61.64, and 66.0301, the
Members enter into this Agreement to create the District to provide on behalf of the Members
emergency medical services (EMS) within the District Territory, subject to the terms of this
Agreement.
III. MEMBER RESPONSIBILITIES & POWERS.
A. The Members shall create a District Board to oversee the operation of the
District. The Members shall have the following powers.
B. Each Member shall appoint one director to the District Board. The term of
each Director shall be two years, and a director may serve up to eight years.
Each director serves at the will of the appointing Member and may be
replaced by the Member without cause. Alternate Directors may also be
appointed by the respective Member, who may vote in the absence of the
Director. In the event of the expiration of the term, removal, death or
resignation of a District Board Member, the Member who appointed that
District Board Member shall appoint a replacement member to fill the
remaining term of that District Board Member.
C. Members shall have the sole authority to amend any provisions of this
Agreement. Any such amendment shall require the approval of each
Member.
D. Members shall have the sole authority to approve all annual Operating
Budgets recommended by the District Board.
E. Each annual operating budget shall be approved by all Members. Each
Member who does not approve the proposed annual operating budget, shall
provide the other Members and the District Board with written notice of non-
approval. Such written notice of non-approval shall include all the reasons for
non-approval along with an alternate proposed annual operating budget. The
District Board may amend the proposed annual operating budget and resubmit
it to the Members for approval. If the objecting Member still does not agree to
the revised proposed operating budget after the revision is presented, then a
majority vote of the Members shall approve the budget for the ensuing year.
F. Members shall have the responsibility to fund each approved annual
Operating Budget as determined by their proportionate share of such
Operating Budget, allocated on the equalized valuation of each Member
Town as a percent of the total equalized valuation of the District . Payments
shall be made in four equal installments in January, April, July, and October.
G. Members shall have the sole authority to approve and fund, including
through their own financing, all Capital Expenditures as they determine
appropriate or as recommended by the District Board. To the extent that
one or more Members do not approve a recommended Capital
Expenditure, the process as outlined in III E. shall be used to reach
agreement on Capital Expenditures.
H. Members may delegate to the District Board authority to own facilities,
vehicles, and other property to facilitate managing the District to provide
safe and efficient service for the District.
I. The District Board shall interview and recommend a candidate and terms
of employment for the position of Chief of the District to the Members.
Members shall approve the hiring and terms of employment of Chief of the
District.
J. Members shall have the sole authority, acting unanimously, to admit
additional municipalities as new Members of the District as provided by
one of the procedures in appendix A.
K. Members shall have sole authority, by majority vote, to terminate a member
of the District as provided by one of the procedures in appendix B.
L. Members shall hold an annual meeting no later than September 1st of each
year, the exact time and date to be determined at the previous year’s annual
meeting. The Members shall approve next year’s operating budget and
conduct such other business as may be required. Members may call special
meetings as required.
IV NEMSD DISTRICT BOARD OF DIRECTORS
A. The District Board shall consist of four voting members. It shall elect from its
members the following officers.
B. The Chairperson shall preside at all meetings of the Board, see that orders and
resolutions of the Board are carried out, and sign legal documents as authorized
by the Members.
C. The Vice-Chairperson shall act in the place of the Chairperson in the event of his
or her absence, inability or refusal to act, and shall exercise and perform such
other duties as may be directed by the Board.
D. The Secretary shall oversee the recording of Board votes, keep minutes for all
meetings and procedures of the Board, verify that board meeting notices are
legally posted, and perform such other duties as may be directed by the District
Board.
E. The Treasurer shall oversee collection and investment of district funds, prepare
financial reports and other accounting reports with the assistance of the Chief.
F. The Board shall meet monthly on the (TBD) of the month; Special meetings may
be called by the Chairperson or a majority vote of the Board on at least 5 days
prior notice.
G. At least three of the voting District Board members then serving shall constitute a
quorum, whether in person or via Zoom or other electronic means.
H. The vote of each District Board member shall count as one vote for a total of four
votes. If a quorum of the District Board is present, then a majority of the votes
represented at the meeting, counted as provided, will be the act of the District
Board.
V. DISTRICT BOARD REPONSIBILITIES & POWERS.
A. The powers of the District Board are limited to those powers expressly granted by
this agreement and subject to the terms of this agreement.
B. The District Board shall carry out the provisions of this agreement consistent with
the provisions of the agreement. The District Board may adopt such rules and
regulations as are necessary to carry out its responsibilities provided; they are
consistent with Wisconsin State Statutes and the terms of this agreement.
C. The District Board shall be responsible for monitoring the day-to-day
operational expenses related to the maintenance of all equipment and facilities owned
or leased by the District subject to any conditions imposed by the Members.
D. The District Board shall maintain complete and accurate records of all income
and expenditures arising from operation of the District and hire a reputable certified
public accounting firm experienced in conducting municipal audits to prepare an annual
report on the District operations to present to the annual meeting.
E. The District Board shall set billing fees for ambulance and other services provided
by the District.
F . The District Board shall approve staff salaries and benefits consistent with the
operating budget.
G. The District Board shall approve any contracts necessary for operation of the
District.
H. The District Board may retain legal counsel to advise the board on matters
pertaining to operation of the District.
I. The District Board shall maintain adequate property and casualty, liability, and
workers compensation insurance on all personnel and property owned or leased by the
District.
J. The District Board shall prepare an annual operating budget to submit to the
Members at their annual meeting for approval.
K. The District Board may create committees to work on assigned tasks and projects
as needed. Each committee shall be chaired by a District Board director. Additional
members may be appointed by the District Board.
Appendix A New Members
Admission. The Members by unanimous vote may admit a new Member to the NEMSD.
Such new Members shall agree to all the terms of this Intermunicipal Agreement.
Purchase Requirements. Each new member shall be liable for the purchase of an
ownership share of the NEMSD assets. Assets shall be valued by the Members at their
fair market value as of the date of new Member entry. The Members, at their discretion,
may defer payment of such amounts upon such terms and conditions as may be
approved by unanimous vote of the Members.
Appendix B Termination
Voluntary. Any Member may terminate Membership in the District by giving written notice of
termination to the Secretary of the District. Membership shall terminate at the end of the
following calendar year of the year they made their request. They shall be responsible for their
share of the operating budget through that calendar year and their share of any capital
indebtedness until such time as it is paid.
Ejectment. Any Member that fails to pay its assessed share of the approved operating budget on
or before the due date of any year shall be in default. Unless the default is cured by full payment
of all amounts due within 30 days of mailing of notice thereof to the defaulting Member, service
to the defaulting Member shall cease 90 days after the default. In the event of termination of
service, the defaulting Member shall remain liable for its assessed share of operating budget for
the entire year of termination plus the following calendar year together with interest at the
annual rate of 12% until paid. They shall also be responsible for their share of any capital
indebtedness until such time as it is paid.
Contract for Service. The District Board by unanimous vote may recommend for approval
contracts for service with non-member municipalities or other non-participating groups for
unanimous approval by the Members. Such contracting parties shall be known as Subscribers,
Through such contracts the NEMSD may provide Services to a Subscriber for a set annual fee.
A Subscriber of the Service would hold no ownership interest in any assets of the District,
would have no voting rights at Annual Meetings, and would not be entitled to representation on
the District Board. No contract for service may be entered, if it would impair the ability of the
NEMSD to provide ambulance service to the original Members of the District.
VI. SIGNATURE PAGE

and Winchester, of Vilas County, Wisconsin, by their respective Town Boards, have
authorized their Chairperson and Clerk to sign this Agreement providing for the joint
operation and maintenance of the Northwoods Emergency Medical Services District.

ORDINANCE NO. 2026-03
PUBLIC RECORDS REQUEST PROCEDURE
SECTION I – PURPOSE
The purpose of this ordinance is to establish the procedure by which members of the public
may request access to or copies of public records of the Town of Winchester, to define the
rights and responsibilities of requesters and the legal custodian, and to ensure that the Town of
Winchester fulfills its obligations under the Wisconsin Public Records Law in a consistent,
transparent, and timely manner.
Policy Statement
It is the policy of the Town of Winchester that all persons are entitled to the greatest possible
information regarding the affairs of the town government and the official acts of its officers and
employees. Access to public records shall be presumed complete and shall be denied only in
exceptional cases where a specific statutory exemption, common law limitation, or overriding
public interest in confidentiality applies. Denial of public access is generally contrary to the public
interest. — Wis. Stat. § 19.31
SECTION II – AUTHORITY
The Town Board of the Town of Winchester enacts this ordinance pursuant to the following
statutory authorities:
A. Wis. Stat. §§ 19.31–19.39, the Wisconsin Public Records Law, which establishes the right
of public access to government records and the procedures governing that access.
B. Wis. Stat. § 19.34(1), which requires each authority to adopt, prominently display, and
make available for inspection at its offices a notice containing a description of its

organization, the established times and places at which, the legal custodian from whom,
and the methods whereby the public may obtain information and access to records, make
requests, or obtain copies, and the costs thereof.
C. Wis. Stat. § 19.35(3), which authorizes municipalities to establish fees for reproduction
of public records.
D. Wis. Stat. § 60.10(2)(c), which grants the town board general authority to enact
ordinances for the regulation of town affairs.
SECTION III – DEFINITIONS
As used in this ordinance:
A. “Public record” means any record of the Town of Winchester, as defined in Wis. Stat. §
19.32(2), regardless of the form or format in which it exists.
B. “Legal custodian” means the Town Clerk of the Town of Winchester, who is the legal
custodian of his or her records and the records of the office by operation of Wis. Stat. §
19.33(1), and as further designated by Town Ordinance 2026-[NUMBER].
C. “Requester” means any person, organization, or entity making a request for access to or
copies of public records.
D. “Authority” means the Town of Winchester as a governmental body subject to the
Wisconsin Public Records Law.
E. “Working day” means any day on which the Clerk’s Office is open for business,
excluding weekends and legal holidays.
SECTION IV – HOW TO SUBMIT A REQUEST
A. Requests for public records may be submitted by any of the following methods:
1. In person at Town Hall, 7228 CTH W, Winchester, WI 54557, during office hours.
2. By email to clerk@winchester.wi.gov.
3. By mail addressed to the Town Clerk, Town of Winchester, 7228 CTH W,

SECTION V – RESPONSE TIMEFRAME
A. The legal custodian shall respond to all public records requests as promptly as practicable
and without unreasonable delay, consistent with Wis. Stat. § 19.35(4).
B. For routine requests, the legal custodian shall provide a substantive response within ten
(10) working days of receipt of the request. A substantive response shall be one of the
following:
1. Fulfillment of the request, in whole or in part.
2. Written notice that additional time is needed and the reason therefor, with an
estimated completion date.
3. Written denial of the request, in whole or in part, with the specific legal basis for the
denial.
C. For requests involving a large volume of records, records requiring legal review, or
records that are not readily accessible, the legal custodian shall notify the requester within
five (5) working days acknowledging receipt of the request and providing an estimated
timeframe for fulfillment.

A. The legal custodian may require prepayment of estimated fees for requests anticipated to

B. Fees may be waived or reduced at the discretion of the legal custodian where the

C. No fee may be charged for inspection of records that does not involve copying.
SECTION VIII – LIMITATIONS ON ACCESS
Access to public records may be limited or denied only in the following circumstances,
consistent with Wis. Stat. §§ 19.35 and 19.36:
A. A state or federal statute specifically exempts the record from disclosure.
B. A court has established a common law limitation on access to the record.
C. The legal custodian, after consultation with legal counsel where appropriate, determines
that the public interest in withholding the record clearly outweighs the public interest in
disclosure. This balancing test shall be applied narrowly and documented in writing.
D. The following categories of records are specifically identified as subject to limitation
under Wisconsin law and shall be evaluated on a case-by-case basis:
1. Records containing personally identifiable information protected under state or
federal law.
2. Records related to pending or reasonably anticipated litigation.
3. Records subject to attorney-client privilege.
4. Draft documents not circulated for comment or distributed outside the authority.
5. Any other record for which a specific statutory exemption applies.
E. When access is limited to only a portion of a record, the legal custodian shall provide
access to the non-exempt portions and shall clearly identify the basis for any redaction.

SECTION IX – DENIAL OF REQUEST
A. Any denial of a public records request, in whole or in part, shall be made in writing and
shall include:
1. A statement that the request is denied.
2. The specific legal basis for the denial, including citation to the applicable statute,
common law principle, or public interest determination.
3. Notice of the requester’s right to seek review of the denial under Wis. Stat. § 19.37.
B. No record may be destroyed after a request for that record has been made and before the
request has been granted, or within sixty (60) days after denial of a request, consistent
with Wis. Stat. § 19.21.
C. A requester who believes a request has been improperly denied may seek enforcement
under Wis. Stat. § 19.37, including mandamus action, complaint to the District
Attorney, or action in circuit court.
SECTION X – RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER ORDINANCES
A. This ordinance shall be read in conjunction with Town Ordinance 2020-03
(Preservation/Destruction of Town Records), which governs retention periods and the
destruction of obsolete records.
B. This ordinance shall be read in conjunction with the Town of Winchester Records
Custodian Designation Ordinance, which designates the legal custodian of town records.
C. In the event of any conflict between this ordinance and any other town ordinance, the
provision affording the greater public access to records shall prevail, consistent with the
presumption of complete public access established by Wis. Stat. § 19.31.
SECTION XI – PENALTY
For violations of the Wisconsin Public Records Law, the Town of Winchester adopts the
penalty provisions of Wis. Stat. § 19.21(3), which provide for forfeiture of not less than $25.00
nor more than $200.00 for each violation by any person who fails to comply with the
requirements of this ordinance or the Wisconsin Public Records Law, in addition to any other
civil or criminal liability provided by law.

General Records Schedule
Information Technology and Related Records
Approved by the Public Records Board:
September 8, 2025
Expiration: September 8, 2035
For use by all units of Wisconsin Government at the State, County, and Municipal level
1 | P a g e
I. Scope
This schedule governs the records retention obligations of state agencies pursuant to Wis. Stat. § 16.61, and applies to “public records”
as defined in Wis. Stat. § 16.61(2)(b). These “public records” are referred to as “records” in this schedule.
This General Records Schedule (GRS) covers records which most state agencies, including the University of Wisconsin System
Administration, the University of Wisconsin Institutions, all Wisconsin counties, municipalities and other units of local government create
and use to administer information technology records. Pursuant to the GRS Policy, the implementation of said schedules by Wisconsin
state agencies is mandatory and immediate. Implementation of a GRS by the UW System Administration, all UW campuses, all
Wisconsin counties, municipalities or other local units of government is optional but recommended. Adopting the schedule does not
require local units to begin creating any record series that they currently do not produce.
INTENTIONAL OMISSIONS
Automated Applications
IT holds records and facilitates data processing and the web presentation of business records for the customers they serve. As a result,
IT is not the owner of customer business records. Program and system application records are covered by separate Records
Retention/Disposition Authorizations (RDAs) or other General Records Schedules (GRS) based on the business needs of the area
responsible for the related program or system application.
• Computer Applications
The data collected and processed by, and output from, computer applications belongs to programs and must be scheduled by the
program. IT may facilitate the retention and disposition of that data as documented in the program RDA.
• Web Content/Social Media
This GRS does not address business records presented on the internet/intranet or in social media. Subject matter experts (i.e., program
or business area staff) are the content owners and have the responsibility for scheduling and retaining those records to meet the
program business needs.
Backup Processes
A “backup” process refers to making copies of original data so the copies are available for a restore if the original data is lost. Those
additional copies are typically called "backups." Backups are used for two reasons: 1) to restore a computer/server to an operational
state following a major loss of data (disaster recovery) and 2) to restore files that have been accidentally deleted or corrupted.
Backups are not designed to be used for records retention. In those cases where agencies are currently depending on backups for
records retention purposes, the backups must be scheduled for the longest retention period of any information carried on the medium.
Retained backups may be subject to discovery or public records requests.
2 | P a g e
This general schedule may not include records which are unique to the mission of a single government unit. Records that are unique to
the mission of a specific government unit require a separate Records Disposition Authorization (RDA). The government unit is
responsible for creating a RDA(s) that must be submitted to, and approved by, the Public Records Board (PRB).
This schedule goes into effect upon final approval by the Public Records Board.
II. Introduction to General Records Schedules
See the Introduction to General Records Schedules for additional information about how to use this schedule. In particular, please
review the restrictions on conditions that might preclude the authorized destruction of documents in the normal course of business
including open records requests, ongoing legal holds, or audits currently underway or known to be planned. Also included in the
Introduction to GRSs you will find further information on: Who May Use GRSs, Records Responsibilities, Records Format, Retaining
Records, Confidential and Personally Identifiable Information, and Understanding the GRS Categories. You should review this
document before implementing a GRS.
Adopting a General Records Schedule - Submit the original and two copies of the Notification of General Schedules Adoption
Form (PRB-002) to:
State Archivist
Wisconsin Historical Society
816 State St.
Madison, WI 53706
The Wisconsin Public Records Board (PRB) will acknowledge your Notification of Adoption by returning a signed copy of the
adoption to the submitting entity.
III. Records Format
Records covered in this schedule may be in paper, electronic, or other formats. Electronic format examples include those created or
transmitted via e-mail, data contained in database systems, and tapes/cartridges. To safeguard the information contained in records
maintained exclusively in electronic format, agencies must meet the standards and requirements for the management of electronic
records outlined in Wis. Admin. Code ch. Admin 12.
IV. Personally Identifiable Information
Wisconsin law requires authorities to specifically identify certain record series within a general records schedule that contain Personally
Identifiable Information (PII). Wisconsin Stat. § 19.62(5) defines PII broadly as “information that can be associated with a particular
individual through one or more identifiers or other information or circumstances.” Despite this broad definition, Wis. Stat. §
16.61(3)(u)(2) , requires that record series within a schedule containing the following types of PII need not be identified as such: a) the
3 | P a g e
results of certain computer matching programs; b) mailing lists; c) telephone or e-mail directories; d) record series pertaining exclusively
to agency employees; and e) record series that contains PII incidental to the primary purpose for which the records series was created,
and f) those relating to state agency procurement or budgeting. If in doubt as to whether a specific record series contains PII, check
with your agency legal counsel.
V. Confidentiality of Records
Most records are not confidential and are open to public disclosure, however, there are exceptions. This GRS will identify any record
series that may contain information required by law to be kept confidential or specifically required to be protected from public access,
identifying the state or federal statute, administrative rule, or other legal authority that so requires. If in doubt as to whether or not a
specific record, or content in that record, is confidential, check with your agency legal counsel. A record series should be identified as
confidential even if not all records in the series contain confidential information and not all parts of records covered by the series are
confidential.
VI. Wisconsin Historical Society Notification
Wis. Stat. § 19.21(4) requires that all county and municipal public records must be offered for transfer to the Wisconsin Historical
Society (WHS) 60 days prior to their destruction. If the disposition of a record series is “destroy” or “destroy confidential”, this indicates
the WHS has waived notification and the records can be destroyed. If the disposition of a record series is “transfer to WHS”, this
indicates notification to the WHS is required prior to destruction. Information on transferring records and proper handling of obsolete
records can be found on the Society’s webpage .
VII. Informational Tables
Superseded Record Series
“Superseded” means that a new record series or RDA number has been used to cover records that were previously identified
differently. The last column in the following GRS table titled “Previous RDA Number (if applicable)” provides a cross walk between new
and any superseded RDA numbers. When revising a GRS, an attempt is made to retain the previous RDA number, providing the
underlying records remain the same.
Related Records
The “Related Records Series” section provides information on other record series in approved GRSs which may relate to the broader
functional area of this GRS. These record series are listed to facilitate a more complete understanding of all the record series within the
broad scope of this function of government. It may not however contain a complete listing of all records series used within your agency
for these types of business records. See the “Related Records Series” section included in this document.
Closed Record Series
4 | P a g e
When revising a GRS, it is common for some previously included record series to be closed. The “Closed Series” section lists series
containing records that are no longer created, nor are they expected to be in the future. See the “Closed Series” section included in this
document.
Revision History
See the “Revision History” section for a listing of changes to this GRS.

This schedule goes into effect upon final approval by the Public Records Board.
II. Records Format
Records covered in this schedule may be in paper, electronic, or other formats. Electronic format examples include those created or
transmitted via e-mail, data contained in database systems, and tapes/cartridges. To safeguard the information contained in records
maintained exclusively in electronic format, agencies must meet the standards and requirements for the management of electronic
records outlined in Wis. Admin. Code ch. Admin 12.
III. Personally Identifiable Information
Wisconsin law requires authorities to specifically identify certain record series within a general records schedule that contain Personally
Identifiable Information (PII). Wisconsin Stat. § 19.62(5) defines PII broadly as “information that can be associated with a particular
individual through one or more identifiers or other information or circumstances.” Despite this broad definition, Wis. Stat. §
16.61(3)(u)(2) , requires that record series within a schedule containing the following types of PII need not be identified as such: a) the
results of certain computer matching programs; b) mailing lists; c) telephone or e-mail directories; d) record series pertaining exclusively
to agency employees; and e) record series that contains PII incidental to the primary purpose for which the records series was created,
and f) those relating to state agency procurement or budgeting. If in doubt as to whether a specific record series contains PII, check
with your agency legal counsel.

IV. Confidentiality of Records
Most records are not confidential and are open to public disclosure, however, there are exceptions. This GRS will identify any record
series that may contain information required by law to be kept confidential or specifically required to be protected from public access,
identifying the state or federal statute, administrative rule, or other legal authority that so requires. If in doubt as to whether or not a
specific record, or content in that record, is confidential, check with your agency legal counsel. A record series should be identified as
confidential even if not all records in the series contain confidential information and not all parts of records covered by the series are
confidential.
V. Superseded Record Series
“Superseded” means that a new record series or RDA number has been used to cover records that were previously identified
differently. The last column in the following GRS table titled “Previous RDA Number (if applicable)” provides a cross walk between new
and any superseded RDA numbers. When revising a GRS, an attempt is made to retain the previous RDA number, providing the
underlying records remain the same.
VI. Related Records
The “Related Records Series” section provides information on other record series in approved GRSs which may relate to the broader
functional area of this GRS. These record series are listed to facilitate a more complete understanding of all the record series within the
broad scope of this function of government. It may not however contain a complete listing of all records series used within your agency
for these types of business records. See the “Related Records Series” section included in this document.
VII. Closed Record Series
When revising a GRS it is common for some previously included record series to be closed. The “Closed Series” section lists series
containing records that are no longer created, nor are they expected to be in the future. See the “Closed Series” section included in this
document.
VIII. Revision History
See the “Revision History” section for a listing of changes to this GRS.

● Purpose and Scope
This policy establishes procedures for the issuance, tracking, and return of physical keys and electronic
access codes for all Town of Winchester facilities available for public reservation. It applies to all
individuals and organizations that reserve Town facilities under the Town of Winchester Facility Use
Policy (Policy 2026-01) and to all Town staff authorized to administer keys and access codes.
1. Facilities and Access Types
All Town of Winchester rental facilities use physical key sets and electronic keypad locks.
2. Authorized Personnel
Only the Town Clerk and Deputy Clerk are authorized to issue physical keys, assign keypad access
codes, and maintain the Key and Access Code Log. No other Town employee, officer, or volunteer
may issue keys or codes without explicit written authorization from the Town Clerk, with the
exception of the Library Director for library-related programs.

3. Key Issuance
3.1 Eligibility
Keys will be issued only to the applicant named on the approved Facility Use Request Form and Key
Issuance Receipt. Keys may not be transferred to another individual. The applicant must present a
valid photo ID at time of pickup.
3.2 Pickup Location and Timing
Keys may be picked up no sooner than two (2) days before the scheduled event. Keys may be picked
up at the following locations, subject to staff availability and current office hours:
• Town Hall Clerk’s Office (7228 CTH W, Winchester)
• Lockbox located on the front door handle of Town Hall
4. Keypad Access Codes
4.1 Activation and Deactivation
Access codes shall be activated no later than four (4) hours before the scheduled start of the event.
Codes shall be deactivated the day following the event. The Clerk’s Office is responsible for
programming and deactivating all codes (exception: Library Director for Library programs).
4.2 Code Confidentiality
Access codes are issued solely for use during the approved rental period. The applicant is responsible
for ensuring the code is not shared beyond those participating in the reserved event. Because codes are
automatically deactivated after each rental period, unauthorized sharing does not create a standing
security risk; however, intentional misuse may be treated as a policy violation at the discretion of the
Town Clerk.

5. Key Return
5.1 Return Deadline
All physical keys must be returned as soon as possible following the event and no later than two days
after the event ends. Prompt return of keys is a condition of security deposit refund.
5.2 Return Locations
Keys may be returned at any of the following locations:
• In person at the Town Hall Clerk’s Office during regular business hours
• Lockbox located at the front door of Town Hall
• Drop box to the left of the front door of Town Hall (available 24 hours)
5.3 Deposit Conditions
Return of all issued keys is a condition of security deposit refund under the Town’s Facility Use
Policy. The security deposit will not be released until all keys have been confirmed returned. If a key is
not returned, costs associated with re-keying or lock replacement will be deducted from the deposit in
addition to any other applicable charges.
6. Unreturned and Lost Keys
If a key has not been returned by the second day following the event, the Clerk’s Office will contact
the applicant to arrange immediate return. If the key remains unreturned after ten (10) business days
from the date of first contact, the Town will withhold the security deposit in full and assess the
applicant for actual re-keying or lock replacement costs. The applicant is responsible for all costs
regardless of the cause of the loss.

7. Violations and Privilege Revocation
Violations of this policy — including but not limited to failure to return keys, loss of keys, or misuse of
access codes or the facility itself — will be tracked in the Key and Access Code Log for both individual
renters and any organizations on whose behalf they reserved. An individual or organization that
accumulates three (3) violations under this policy or the Town’s Facility Use Policy (combined) may
have facility rental privileges revoked at the discretion of the Town Board. Each violation will be
documented and the applicant notified in writing by the Clerk’s Office.
8. Amendment and Review
This policy may be amended by Town Board resolution. The Clerk’s Office is responsible for
maintaining the current version and ensuring it remains consistent with the Town’s Facility Use Policy
(Policy 2026-01).

ADOPTION OF THE WISCONSIN MUNICIPAL RECORDS SCHEDULE
(WMRS)
WHEREAS, Wisconsin Statute § 19.21(1) defines public records as all property and things
received from an officer’s predecessor or other persons and required by law to be filed,
deposited, or kept in the officer’s office, or which are in the lawful possession or control of the
officer or the officer’s deputies; and
WHEREAS, Wisconsin Statute § 19.21(4) requires municipalities to adopt ordinances
establishing records retention schedules, and provides that unless a shorter period is approved
by the Wisconsin Public Records Board (PRB), records may not be destroyed until they ha ve
been retained for a minimum of seven (7) years; and
WHEREAS, the Wisconsin Public Records Board, in coordination with the Wisconsin
Historical Society, has approved the Wisconsin Municipal Records Schedule (WMRS), a
general records schedule designed for use by Wisconsin municipalities, which establishes
legally compliant minimum retention periods for the full range of records commonly
generated by municipal governments; and
WHEREAS, the current WMRS was approved by the PRB on August 27, 2018, and is valid
through August 27, 2028; and

cost-effective records management, reduce storage burden, and ensure accountability and
transparency to the public; and

to initiate the WMRS adoption process without delay.

administrative steps to facilitate submission of Form PRB-002, including providing any

Approval by the Public Records Board:

For use by all units of Wisconsin Government at the State, County, and Municipal level
1 | P a g e
I. Scope
This schedule governs the records retention obligations of state agencies pursuant to Wis. Stat. § 16.61, and applies to “public records”
as defined in Wis. Stat. § 16.61(2)(b). These “public records” are referred to as “records” in this schedule.
This General Records Schedule (GRS) covers records which most state agencies, including the University of Wisconsin System
Administration, the University of Wisconsin Institutions, all Wisconsin counties, municipalities and other units of local government create
and use to administer purchasing and procurement related records. Pursuant to the GRS Policy, the implementation of said schedules
by Wisconsin state agencies is mandatory and immediate. Implementation of a GRS by the UW System Administration, all UW
campuses, all Wisconsin counties, municipalities or other local units of government is optional but recommended. Adopting the
schedule does not require local units to begin creating any record series that they currently do not produce.
This general schedule may not include records which are unique to the mission of a single government unit. Records that are unique to
the mission of a specific government unit require a separate Records Disposition Authorization (RDA). The government unit is
responsible for creating a RDA(s) that must be submitted to, and approved by, the Public Records Board (PRB).
This schedule goes into effect upon final approval by the Public Records Board.
II. Introduction to General Records Schedules
See the Introduction to General Records Schedules for additional information about how to use this schedule. In particular, please
review the restrictions on conditions that might preclude the authorized destruction of documents in the normal course of business
including open records requests, ongoing legal holds, or audits currently underway or known to be planned. Also included in the
Introduction to GRSs you will find further information on: Who May Use GRSs, Records Responsibilities, Records Format, Retaining
Records, Confidential and Personally Identifiable Information, and Understanding the GRS Categories. You should review this
document before implementing a GRS.
Adopting a General Records Schedule - Submit the original and two copies of the Notification of General Schedules Adoption
Form (PRB-002) to:
State Archivist
Wisconsin Historical Society
816 State St.
Madison, WI 53706
The Wisconsin Public Records Board (PRB) will acknowledge your Notification of Adoption by returning a signed copy of the
adoption to the submitting entity.

III. Records Format
Records covered in this schedule may be in paper, electronic, or other formats. Electronic format examples include those created or
transmitted via e-mail, data contained in database systems, and tapes/cartridges. To safeguard the information contained in records
maintained exclusively in electronic format, agencies must meet the standards and requirements for the management of electronic
records outlined in Wis. Admin. Code ch. Admin 12.
IV. Personally Identifiable Information
Wisconsin law requires authorities to specifically identify certain record series within a general records schedule that contain Personally
Identifiable Information (PII). Wisconsin Stat. § 19.62(5) defines PII broadly as “information that can be associated with a particular
individual through one or more identifiers or other information or circumstances.” Despite this broad definition, Wis. Stat. §
16.61(3)(u)(2) , requires that record series within a schedule containing the following types of PII need not be identified as such: a) the
results of certain computer matching programs; b) mailing lists; c) telephone or e-mail directories; d) record series pertaining exclusively
to agency employees; and e) record series that contains PII incidental to the primary purpose for which the records series was created,
and f) those relating to state agency procurement or budgeting. If in doubt as to whether a specific record series contains PII, check
with your agency legal counsel.
V. Confidentiality of Records
Most records are not confidential and are open to public disclosure, however, there are exceptions. This GRS will identify any record
series that may contain information required by law to be kept confidential or specifically required to be protected from public access,
identifying the state or federal statute, administrative rule, or other legal authority that so requires. If in doubt as to whether or not a
specific record, or content in that record, is confidential, check with your agency legal counsel. A record series should be identified as
confidential even if not all records in the series contain confidential information and not all parts of records covered by the series are
confidential.
VI. Wisconsin Historical Society Notification
Wis. Stat. § 19.21(4) requires that all county and municipal public records must be offered for transfer to the Wisconsin Historical
Society (WHS) 60 days prior to their destruction. If the disposition of a record series is “destroy” or “destroy confidential”, this indicates
the WHS has waived notification and the records can be destroyed. If the disposition of a record series is “transfer to WHS”, this
indicates notification to the WHS is required prior to destruction. Information on transferring records and proper handling of obsolete
records can be found on the Society’s webpage .

received from an officer’s predecessor or other persons and required by law to be filed,
deposited, or kept in the officer’s office, or which are in the lawful possession or control of the
officer or the officer’s deputies; and

establishing records retention schedules, and provides that unless a shorter period is approved
by the Wisconsin Public Records Board (PRB), records may not be destroyed until they ha ve
been retained for a minimum of seven (7) years; and
WHEREAS, the Wisconsin Public Records Board, in coordination with the Wisconsin
Historical Society, has approved the Wisconsin Municipal Records Schedule (WMRS), a
general records schedule designed for use by Wisconsin municipalities, which establishes
legally compliant minimum retention periods for the full range of records commonly
generated by municipal governments; and
WHEREAS, the current WMRS was approved by the PRB on August 27, 2018, and is valid
through August 27, 2028; and

ORDINANCE 2022-06
DRIVEWAYS ORDINANCE FOR
THE TOWN OF WINCHESTER, VILAS COUNTY WISCONSIN
A. Purpose:
1. Establish the minimum standards for the construction or rebuilding of driveways, private roads, or private
lanes connecting to any public roadways in the Township of Winchester to enable the safe ingress and
egress of Emergency response vehicles, and for purpose of public safety.
2. Regulate the construction or rebuilding of driveways, private roads, or private lanes abutting any
public roadway in Winchester Township.
B. Jurisdiction: Jurisdiction of these regulation shall include all driveways, private roads, or private lanes
within Winchester Township.
C. Authority: This ordinance is enacted to provide general specifications for Town roads, driveways, private
roads, or private lanes in Winchester Township. Pursuant to sections 60.10(2)(c), 60.22(3), 61.34(1) of
Wisconsin State Statutes, and under the controlled access highway power granted pursuant to sections
83.027(10) and 84.25(1) of Wisconsin State Statutes. This Ordinance supersedes Ordinance #2018-02.
D. Driveways/Private roads/Private Lanes abutting public roads:
1. The following provisions apply to private driveways, private roads and private lanes abutting public
roads. All work shall be performed without danger to or interference with traffic using the town road or
street.
a. Unless otherwise stated, a minimum of a twelve (12) inch by twenty-four (24) foot long culvert shall
be installed and maintained by the property owner under the proposed private driveway, road or lane to
provide proper drainage under the entrance and along the public roadway. Fill shall be made over
culverts so that the ends are free and the ends shall be riprapped or sodded to prevent fill material from
spilling into the ditch and clogging the culvert. Work of placing culverts and placing riprap and/or sod
shall proceed diligently and be completed promptly after it is begun and shall present a neat
appearance when completed.

Ordinance 2026-01
Driveway Ordinance
I. TITLE AND PURPOSE
The title of this Ordinance is the Town of Winchester Driveway Ordinance. The
purpose is to regulate, for public health and safety reasons, the establishment,
repair, construction, improvement, modification, and reconstruction of private
driveways, to assure that the methods of repair, construction, improvement,
modification, and reconstruction practices used in any driveway will protect the
public health, safety, and general welfare of persons in the Town of Winchester.
This ordinance does not include normal wear and tear to a driveway and should not
be interpreted to require a permit for normal maintenance.
II. AUTHORITY
The Town Board has the authority under the controlled access highway power
granted pursuant to 66.0425, 83.027(10), 84.25(1) Wis. Stats., to adopt a town
driveway and highway access ordinance and has the general authority under its
village powers under 60.10(2)(c), 60.22(3), and 61.34(1) Wis. Stats., to adopt this
ordinance.
III. ADOPTION AND ABORGATION
A. This Ordinance, adopted by a majority of the town board on a roll call vote
with a quorum present and voting and proper notice having been given,
provides for the regulation by Town Board of certain driveways and private
roads and their access to public roadways in the Town of Winchester.
B. This Ordinance supersedes all prior Town of Winchester Driveway
Ordinances. However, where another ordinance imposes greater restriction,
the provisions of the more restrictive ordinance shall prevail.
IV. DEFINITIONS
A. "Driveway” means any private way, private road, or other avenue of private
travel that runs through any part of a private parcel of land that connects or
will connect with any public roadway and will provide vehicular access from
the public roadway to a residence, business, recreational site, or other
similarly appropriate use including temporary driveways.
20260223 2
B. "Emergency Vehicle" means any fire, police, ambulance, or first responder
vehicle used in emergency of hazard activities in the town.
C. "Town" means the Town of Winchester, Vilas County, Wisconsin.
D. "Town Board" means the board of supervisors for the Town of Winchester,
Vilas County, Wisconsin, and includes any designee of the board authorized
to act for the board.
E. "Town Clerk" means the clerk of the Town of Winchester, Vilas County,
Wisconsin.
F. “Permit" means the Town of Winchester Driveway Permit
G. "Wis. stats." means the Wisconsin Statutes, including successor provisions
to cited statutes.
V. COVERAGE
A. This Ordinance applies to all driveways which occur or are proposed to
occur in the Town of Winchester, Vilas County, Wisconsin.
B. A new private road providing access to more than three residences may have
separate requirements found in the Town of Winchester Road Ordinance.
Private roads not built to the Town road standards cannot be considered for
transfer to the Town and must be brought up to Town standards before being
transferred.
C. No person may establish or construct a driveway or reconstruct, reroute, or
alter the existing slope of any existing driveway without first obtaining a
permit from the Town Board.
D. Any person prior to and at the time of seeking a driveway permit must own or
have legal interest in and current legal access to the land to which the permit
will apply.
E. Driveways accessing onto a County Highway must obtain approval from the
proper authority, Vilas County Zoning and Planning Department.
VI. SPECIFICATIONS
A. All work shall be performed without danger to or interference with traffic
using a public roadway.
B. Town road surfaces, slopes, shoulders, ditches, and vegetation disturbed by
work on a driveway shall be restored by the property owner.
C. All costs of installation and maintenance of culverts as well as public
roadway restoration shall be the sole responsibility of the property owner.
20260223 3
D. All fees for installation and maintenance of signs and signposts for fire
numbers, addresses, and road or driveway identification names shall be the
sole responsibility of the property owner.
E. All installation and maintenance of signage shall be completed by the Town
crew.
F. The edge of all new driveways and private roads shall be located at least five
feet from the nearest side lot line except in the case of a driveway abutting a
public road and providing access to two adjacent parcels. Said driveway can
be on the lot line or split between parcels. A maintenance agreement and
easement agreement must be recorded at the Vilas County Register of
Deeds.
G. Driveways for a single property require:
1. A roadbed of twelve feet in width
2. An unobstructed overhead clearance of fifteen feet for ingress and
egress of Emergency Vehicles
3. Graveling to a minimum width of twelve feet with a minimum of four
inches of compacted gravel over an appropriate base with sufficient
drainage.
4. It is recommended to build the driveway with a big enough space to
accommodate the ingress and egress of Emergency Vehicles.
H. Private roads for more than one property require the following:
1. A minimum easement of twenty feet
2. Plus, all the requirements of a single property driveway.
I. Bridges must be inspected and rated to pass a thirty five ton fire apparatus
safely and to have a minimum width of ten feet. Bridges must be certified by
a licensed Professional Engineer in the State of Wisconsin.
J. A fifty foot diameter turn around on all new or reconstructed private roads. If
space is not available for a fifty foot diameter turn around, adjacent
landowners must try to establish the largest possible turn to be built in the
space available.
K. Unless otherwise stated, a minimum of twelve inch diameter by twenty-four
foot long culvert installed and maintained by the property owner under the
proposed driveway to provide proper drainage under the entrance and along
the public roadway
1. Fill shall not cover the ends of the culvert
2. Both culvert ends shall be riprapped or sodded to prevent fill material
from spilling into the ditch and clogging the culvert
20260223 4
3. The work of placing culverts and riprap/sod shall proceed diligently
and be completed promptly after it is begun and shall present a neat
appearance when completed.
L. Entryways within fifty feet of the centerline of any public roadway shall not
exceed a five percent up or down slope. However, when existing property
slopes exceed ten percent the Town Board may allow entryway slope to be
increased to minimize grading damage to the property, but in no case shall
entryways exceed fifteen percent up or down slope and entryways exceeding
ten percent shall provide rounding at the intersection with the public road to
prevent rear-end or mid-wheel dragging to vehicles entering or leaving the
property
M. Driveways should align with the public roadway at right angles to facilitate
turning moves from both directions and entryways should not be located
adjacent to sharp vertical or horizontal curves in the public roadway but shall
be in positions where adequate stopping sight is available to all vehicles.
N. Unless otherwise documented, the Town road right-of-way at the place of
construction is assumed to extend thirty-three feet from the centerline of the
Town road.
O. Permits for temporary driveways/roadways shall require the permit holder to
return the affected area to its natural state within six months after use is
halted.
P. Prior to the transfer of a private road to the Town of Winchester, the road
must meet all the requirements and specifications of a Town blacktopped
road.
Q. All work shall be carried out to the satisfaction of the Town Board in
compliance with any and all permits.
R. The applicant is financially responsible for any and all damage caused to
town roads as a result of any work done pursuant to the driveway permit.
S. Failure to maintain driveways to the minimum standards listed in Paragraph
VI could result in the inability of emergency vehicles to provide prompt and
effective emergency services to private properties in the Town of Winchester.
VII. APPLICATION AND PERMIT PROVISIONS
A. An application for the Town of Winchester Driveway Permit is available from
the Town Clerk or on the Town website.
B. The permit applicant shall submit to the Town Clerk a completed application
for each permit with the appropriate fee and with the following attachments:
20260223 5
1. Sketch map: A rough sketch showing the conceptual area of the
project and approximate location and dimensions of the project. The
sketch map may be submitted to the Town Board prior to the
submission of the other supporting documents for the Town Board to
provide initial comments and review of the proposal. Formal approval
for a permit will not be granted without the submission of complete
supporting documents.
2. The Town Board may require other documents to be attached to the
application including but not limited to: plat map, aerial photo/site
analysis, soil/slope analysis, construction plan.
C. In the event a landowner is unable to comply with the requirements of this
ordinance to upgrade an existing driveway, the landowner can petition the
town board for a variance to upgrade the driveway to the extent possible.
D. The Town Board shall approve or deny every permit application and may, as a
condition of issuance, place specific restrictions or conditions on the permit,
which shall require compliance by the permittee.
E. A denial of a permit by the Town Board shall accompany an explanation of
the facts on which the permit has been denied.
F. The applicant may re-apply for the permit at any time after denial, but after
two consecutive denials on the same parcel, another application may not be
considered for sixty days.
G. The applicant shall notify the Town Board in writing via first class mail,
personal delivery, or time stamped electronic mail, within thirty days after
completion of the construction, reconstruction, rerouting, or alteration of
the driveway/driveway access. Within thirty days of notification, the Town
Board or its designee shall conduct an inspection of the driveway to ensure
full compliance with the permit and this ordinance.
H. Permits expire two years after issuance, and all approved construction must
be completed before the permit expires. Each permit may be renewed for a
period of six months. If work is not completed by the end of the six-month
renewal period, a new application and fee must be submitted and approved.
I. Driveway permits will be valid for the original applicant and non-
transferrable.
J. The applicant, their successor, or assignee agrees to hold harmless the
Town of Winchester, its agents and employees, against any action for
personal injury or property damage sustained by reason or exercise of this
permit.
K. The Town, at itssole discretion,may electto enforce violationsofthis
Ordinance pursuanttothe terms oftheTown ofWinchester Citations
Ordinance and the Town of Winchester Penalties, Deposits, and Fees
Ordinance.

Should any portionofthisordinance or the affectedcode section(s)be held invalid
by a court of competent jurisdiction,the remainder shallnot be affected.

This ordinance iseffectiveupon publication or posting.The Town Clerk shall
