Town of Winchester, County of Vilas
Ordinance 2026-04
Boating and Water Regulations Ordinance
20260622
I. TITLE AND PURPOSE
The Winchester Town Board recognizes an ordinance on boating and water regulations to
serve the best interests of public health and safety for the Town
II. AUTHORITY
Wis. Stats 30.50 through 30.99 to the extent applicable are adopted by reference and
regulate the operation and control of all boats on any lake, river, or channel in the Town of
Winchester, Vilas County, Wisconsin and has the general authority under Wis. Stats 60 &
Wis. Stats 61 to adopt this ordinance.
III. SPEED RESTRICTIONS
No person shall operate a motorboat, personal watercraft, or power boat on any lake, river
or channel in the Town of Winchester except in compliance with Chapter NR 5, of the
Wisconsin Administrative Code as applicable and as follows:
A. In open waters at a speed which is reasonable and prudent
B. In all rivers or channels at a slow no wake speed
C. No power boat racing without the express permission of the Town Board
IV. WATER SKIING:
A. No person shall operate a motorboat towing a person on water skis, aquaplane or similar
device before sunrise or after sunset.
B. Water skiing or aquaplaning is forbidden in any channel or river in the Town of
Winchester.
C. No person operating a motorboat that is towing persons engaged in water skiing,
aquaplaning or similar activity may operate the motorboat within 100 feet of any
occupied anchored boat, any personal watercraft or any marked swimming area or public
boat landing.
D. No person who is engaged in water skiing, aquaplaning or similar activity may operate
within 100 feet of a personal watercraft or allow the tow rope, while in use, to operate
within 100 feet of a personal watercraft.
E. No person may operate a personal watercraft within 100 feet of any of the following:
i) A motorboat towing a person who is engaged in water skiing, aquaplaning or similar
activities.
ii) The tow rope of a motorboat towing a person who is engaged in water skiing,
aquaplaning or similar activities.
F. A person who is engaged in water skiing, aquaplaning or similar activity.
G. Paragraphs (C) to (E) do not apply to pick up or drop off areas for people engaged in
water skiing, aquaplaning or similar activities.
H. See ordinance 2024-02 Artificial Wakes and 2022-03 Motorboats and Watercraft Joint
ordinance with Presque Isle and 2022-03 and ordinance 2024-07 Papoose Lake artificial
wake ordinance.
Town of Winchester, County of Vilas
Ordinance 2026-04
Boating and Water Regulations Ordinance
20260622
V. HOUSEBOATS:
No person shall operate a houseboat on any lake, river or channel in the Town of Winchester.
A houseboat is defined as a boat or watercraft which provides living quarters for one or more
people. Each day this section is violated shall constitute a separate offense.
VI. MARKING BUOYS
A. No person shall move, tamper with, destroy or attempt to destroy, or moor or fasten any
object to any marking buoy located on any of the public waters in this Town.
B. No person, association, including lake associations, or any other entity may place buoys
in any of the public waters in the Town of Winchester without prior permission from the
DNR and the Town Board.
VII. PERSONEL WATERCRAFT
A. No person shall operate a personal watercraft on any of the public waters of the Town of
Winchester except between sunrise and sunset.
B. Personal watercraft as used in this Ordinance is defined by Section 30.50(9)(d), Wis.
Stats.
VIII. BOAT LANDINGS
IX. Public nudity is prohibited
A. Swimming/Bathing is prohibited at all Town owned watercraft landing.
B. Power launching and loading is prohibited.
X. VIOLATION, LEGAL ACTIONS, AND PENALTIES
A. The Winchester Town Board or its designee shall enforce the Boating and Water
Regulation Ordinance and shall make rulings as to the compliance in questionable or
disputed situations.
B. If any provision of this ordinance is being violated, written notice of such violation shall
be issued indicating the nature of the violation.
C. Persons may appeal in writing with the Town Board within thirty (30) days after receipt of
such notice. Appeals shall be placed on the agenda for the next Town Board meeting.
D. If the violation is not appealed within the thirty (30) day period, actions may be initiated
to collect the penalties for such violations.
E. Any person found to be in violation of this ordinance may be subject to a penalty. See
Town of Winchester penalty and fee schedule.
XI. SEVERABILITY CLAUSE
Should any portion of this ordinance or the affected code section(s) be held invalid by a court
of competent jurisdiction, the remainder shall not be affected.
XII. EFFECTIVE DATE

● Purpose and Scope
This policy establishes procedures for the issuance, tracking, and return of physical keys and electronic
access codes for all Town of Winchester facilities available for public reservation. It applies to all
individuals and organizations that reserve Town facilities under the Town of Winchester Facility Use
Policy (Policy 2026-01) and to all Town staff authorized to administer keys and access codes.
1. Facilities and Access Types
All Town of Winchester rental facilities use physical key sets and electronic keypad locks.
2. Authorized Personnel
Only the Town Clerk and Deputy Clerk are authorized to issue physical keys, assign keypad access
codes, and maintain the Key and Access Code Log. No other Town employee, officer, or volunteer
may issue keys or codes without explicit written authorization from the Town Clerk, with the
exception of the Library Director for library-related programs.
Town of Winchester
7228 CTH W, Winchester, WI 54557
winchesterwi.com | 715-686-2123
Town of Winchester — Facility Use Key and Access Code Management Policy 2026-02 — Page 2
3. Key Issuance
3.1 Eligibility
Keys will be issued only to the applicant named on the approved Facility Use Request Form and Key
Issuance Receipt. Keys may not be transferred to another individual. The applicant must present a
valid photo ID at time of pickup.
3.2 Pickup Location and Timing
Keys may be picked up no sooner than two (2) days before the scheduled event. Keys may be picked
up at the following locations, subject to staff availability and current office hours:
• Town Hall Clerk’s Office (7228 CTH W, Winchester)
• Lockbox located on the front door handle of Town Hall
4. Keypad Access Codes
4.1 Activation and Deactivation
Access codes shall be activated no later than four (4) hours before the scheduled start of the event.
Codes shall be deactivated the day following the event. The Clerk’s Office is responsible for
programming and deactivating all codes (exception: Library Director for Library programs).
4.2 Code Confidentiality
Access codes are issued solely for use during the approved rental period. The applicant is responsible
for ensuring the code is not shared beyond those participating in the reserved event. Because codes are
automatically deactivated after each rental period, unauthorized sharing does not create a standing
security risk; however, intentional misuse may be treated as a policy violation at the discretion of the
Town Clerk.

Town of Winchester — Facility Use Key and Access Code Management Policy 2026-02 — Page 3
5. Key Return
5.1 Return Deadline
All physical keys must be returned as soon as possible following the event and no later than two days
after the event ends. Prompt return of keys is a condition of security deposit refund.
5.2 Return Locations
Keys may be returned at any of the following locations:
• In person at the Town Hall Clerk’s Office during regular business hours
• Lockbox located at the front door of Town Hall
• Drop box to the left of the front door of Town Hall (available 24 hours)
5.3 Deposit Conditions
Return of all issued keys is a condition of security deposit refund under the Town’s Facility Use
Policy. The security deposit will not be released until all keys have been confirmed returned. If a key is
not returned, costs associated with re-keying or lock replacement will be deducted from the deposit in
addition to any other applicable charges.
6. Unreturned and Lost Keys
If a key has not been returned by the second day following the event, the Clerk’s Office will contact
the applicant to arrange immediate return. If the key remains unreturned after ten (10) business days
from the date of first contact, the Town will withhold the security deposit in full and assess the
applicant for actual re-keying or lock replacement costs. The applicant is responsible for all costs
regardless of the cause of the loss.

7. Violations and Privilege Revocation
Violations of this policy — including but not limited to failure to return keys, loss of keys, or misuse of
access codes or the facility itself — will be tracked in the Key and Access Code Log for both individual
renters and any organizations on whose behalf they reserved. An individual or organization that
accumulates three (3) violations under this policy or the Town’s Facility Use Policy (combined) may
have facility rental privileges revoked at the discretion of the Town Board. Each violation will be
documented and the applicant notified in writing by the Clerk’s Office.
8. Amendment and Review
This policy may be amended by Town Board resolution. The Clerk’s Office is responsible for
maintaining the current version and ensuring it remains consistent with the Town’s Facility Use Policy
(Policy 2026-01).

ORDINANCE NO. 2026-05
REQUIRING PERMITS FOR RIGHT-OF-WAY WORK, DRIVEWAY

SECTION I – PURPOSE
This ordinance establishes permit requirements for three categories of activity that affect
Town of Winchester roads and rights-of-way: (a) work performed within a Town road right-
of-way; (b) installation of new driveways connecting to a Town road; and (c) construction of
new roads intended to connect to a Town road, and reconstruction, excavation, or alteration
of any Town road surface by any party other than the Town. The purpose is to protect public
infrastructure, ensure public safety, coordinate work to minimize disruption to residents,
visitors, and wildlife, and provide the public with visibility into permitted projects affecting
Town roads.
SECTION II – AUTHORITY
A. Village powers: s. 60.22, Wis. Stats.
B. Privileges in streets: s. 66.0425, Wis. Stats.
C. Permit requirement for excavations, fill, culverts, or other alterations in highways: s.
86.07, Wis. Stats.

SECTION III – DEFINITIONS
A. Applicant: A person, entity, contractor, or utility applying for a permit under this
ordinance.
B. Driveway: A private roadway providing vehicular access from a Town road to abutting
property.
C. Right-of-Way (ROW): The area within the legally established boundaries of a Town
road, including the roadway surface, shoulders, drainage features, and adjacent lands
controlled by the Town for road purposes.
D. Road Construction: The construction of any new road intended to connect to a Town
road, and the reconstruction, excavation, or surface alteration of any existing Town road
by any party other than the Town.
E. Town Road: Any road under the jurisdiction of the Town of Winchester as maintained
by the Town, excluding state highways and Vilas County highways.
F. Utility Work: Any installation, repair, replacement, or removal of underground or
overhead utility facilities within a Town road right-of-way, including but not limited to
water, sewer, electric, gas, telecommunications, and cable service facilities.
SECTION IV – PERMIT REQUIREMENTS
A. Utility Work Permit. No person shall perform Utility Work within any Town road right -
of-way without first obtaining a Utility Work Permit. The Town Chairperson is
authorized to review and approve Utility Work Permit applications on behalf of the
Town Board.
B. Driveway Permit. No person shall install a new driveway connecting to a Town road
without first obtaining a Driveway Permit. Driveway Permit applications shall be
reviewed and approved by the Town Board at a regular or special meeting. Note:
Driveways connecting to a Vilas County highway are subject to Vilas County approval
and are outside the scope of this ordinance.

C. Road Construction Permit. No person shall undertake Road Construction as defined in
Section III without first obtaining a Road Construction Permit. The Town Chairperson
is authorized to review and approve Road Construction Permit applications on behalf of
the Town Board.
D. Emergencies. In the event of an emergency that threatens life or property, the utility
company shall begin and complete work as efficiently as possible to protect the public
interest. Within 48 hours of the start of the work being performed, the utility company is
to call the Clerk so the permit may be issued retroactively.
SECTION V – ADMINISTRATION
A. Application. Permit applications shall be submitted using the current forms available at
winchesterwi.com/permits and shall include all information required by those forms.
B. Fees. Permit fees are set forth in the Town of Winchester Fee Schedule, as amended from
time to time. Applicants shall consult the current Fee Schedule at the time of application.
C. Public Project Map. All permits issued under this ordinance are aggregated on a public
project map at winchesterwi.com/permits so that residents may remain informed of
active and upcoming projects affecting Town roads and rights-of-way.
SECTION VI – ENFORCEMENT
A. The Town Clerk shall administer this ordinance and maintain records of all permit
applications and issued permits. The Town Chairperson and Town Board shall serve as
the approval authorities as designated in Section IV.
B. Any work performed without a required permit, or in violation of the terms of an issued
permit, may result in the immediate issuance of a stop-work order by the Town
Chairperson or designee. The Town may restore the right-of-way or Town road to its
pre-work condition at the expense of the violator.

Town of Winchester — Address/Fire Number Sign Policy
Policy 2026-04 — Page 2
1. Purpose
This policy establishes the procedure for the issuance, installation, replacement, and fee
structure of address/fire number signs within the Town of Winchester, ensuring that all
properties are clearly and uniformly marked to support emergency response and mail/delivery
services.
2. Eligibility & Requests
• Any member of the public may request an address/fire number sign for a property
within the Town of Winchester.
• An address/fire number sign is issued only after an address number has been assigned by
Vilas County.
3. Issuance & Installation Process
The following process applies to the issuance and installation of all address/fire number signs:
• The Vilas County Clerk assigns the address number and notifies the Town Clerk.
• The Town Clerk orders the sign through Lange Signs, using the Town’s established sign
template.
• The Town crew installs the sign and reports the completed installation back to the Town
Clerk.
• The Town Clerk confirms the completed installation with the Vilas County Clerk.
4. Sign Design Standards
All address/fire number signs shall conform to Vilas County General Code of Ordinances
Chapter 28, Appendix A, including the following:
• Signs shall be oriented horizontally and printed on both sides.
• Signs shall be installed perpendicular to the road.
• Signs shall use white block lettering/numbering, and shall include the name of the Town
(minimum 1 inch high) and the address number (minimum 3½ inches high). Road
names are optional.

• Sign background color shall be blue, green, or red, unless an alternate color is approved
by Vilas County.
• Signs shall be a minimum of 6 inches high and as wide as necessary to accommodate the
required information.
The Town of Winchester currently orders signs through Lange Signs. Clerks shall use the
established sign template for Winchester, which incorporates the Town name and conforms to
County design standards. See the final pages of this document for current design standards.
5. Placement Standards
All address/fire number signs shall be installed in conformance with Vilas County General
Code of Ordinances Chapter 28, Appendix A, including the following:
• Signs shall be securely fastened on U-channel metal posts. Alternate mounting methods
require prior County approval.
• Signs shall be placed on whichever side of the driveway best associates the sign with the
driveway or structure while ensuring maximum visibility.
• Signs shall be located within 20 feet of both the driveway and the road edge, and shall be
installed uniformly throughout the Town. Alternate locations require prior County
approval.
• Signs shall be installed approximately 4½ to 5 feet above road level.
6. Fees
6.1 Initial Installation (New Address)
A fee of $50.00 is assessed for the initial installation of an address/fire number sign for a new
address.

Town of Winchester — Facility Use Refund Requests Policy
Policy 2026-06 — Page 2
1. Purpose
This policy establishes the circumstances under which a facility use fee or security deposit paid
under the Town Facility Use Policy (Policy 2026-01) may be refunded, the process for
requesting and approving a refund, and how approved refunds are issued.
2. Refund Eligibility
A refund of the facility use fee, security deposit, or both may be issued only under one of the
following circumstances:
2.1 Timely Cancellation by the Applicant
Cancellations made at least 7 days prior to the scheduled use are eligible for a full refund of the
use fee and security deposit, consistent with the cancellation terms in Policy 2026-01 § 1.3.
2.2 Town-Initiated Cancellation
If the Town cancels a reservation for any reason — including but not limited to severe
weather, emergency use of the facility, staffing unavailability, or an inadvertent double-
booking — the applicant is eligible for a full refund of the use fee and security deposit,
regardless of how much advance notice was given.
2.3 Unsatisfactory Facility Condition
If the facility was unclean, damaged, or had non-functional equipment or utilities at the time
of use, the applicant may request a full or partial refund of the use fee. The request must
include supporting evidence (such as photographs, a written description of the issue, or
witness accounts) documenting the condition of the facility at the time of use.
3. Non-Qualifying Circumstances
Refunds are not available for cancellations made fewer than 7 days prior to the scheduled use,
except where Section 2.2 applies. In such cases, the use fee is forfeited and the security deposit
is returned, consistent with Policy 2026-01 § 1.3 and § 3.2.

4. Requesting a Refund
• Refund requests must be submitted in writing to the Town Clerk’s Office at
clerk@winchester.wi.gov or 715-686-2123 within 3 days after the scheduled reservation.
• Requests based on unsatisfactory facility condition (Section 2.3) must include
supporting evidence at the time the request is submitted.
• The applicant named on the original Facility Use Agreement must submit the request, or
provide written authorization for another party to do so on their behalf.
5. Approval Process
5.1 Routine Refunds
The Town Clerk is authorized to approve and process refund requests that clearly qualify
under Section 2.1 (timely cancellation) or Section 2.2 (Town-initiated cancellation) without
further Town Board action.
5.2 Exceptions & Disputes
Requests based on unsatisfactory facility condition (Section 2.3), requests that do not clearly
meet the criteria in Section 2, and any disputed refund amount shall be referred to the Town
Board for review and approval at a regular or special meeting.
6. Refund Method
• Approved refunds are issued by Town check or by digital reversal to the original online
payment method.
• No cash refunds are issued, regardless of the original payment method.
• Cash payments approved for refund are issued by Town check.

1. Purpose
This policy establishes a uniform expiration period for checks issued by the Town of
Winchester and a process for handling checks that are not presented for payment within that
period. This policy promotes sound financial management, ensures accurate accoun ting of
Town funds, and protects the Town from liability associated with stale or outstanding checks.
2. Expiration Period
• All checks issued by the Town of Winchester shall be valid for one hundred eighty (180)
days from the date of issuance printed on the check.
• The Town Treasurer is authorized to place a stop payment on any Town-issued check
that remains outstanding 180 days after the date of issuance. This includes currently
outstanding checks that have not been deposited prior to December 24, 2025.
• Expired checks shall not be honored for payment. Any financial institution presenting an
expired Town-issued check for payment does so at its own risk.
3. Reissuance of Expired Checks
3.1 Reissuance Request
• A payee whose Town-issued check has expired may request reissuance by contacting the
Town Clerk’s Office in writing, by email, or in person.
• The reissuance request must include the payee’s name, the original check number, the
check amount, and the original date of issuance.
• The original expired check, if available, must be returned to the Town Clerk’s Office
before a replacement check will be issued. If the original check cannot be located, the
payee must provide a written statement to that effect.
Town of Winchester

Town of Winchester — Facility Use Policy — Page 3
3.2 Processing
• Upon receipt of a valid reissuance request, the Town Clerk shall verify the original
payment record with the Town Treasurer and confirm that a stop payment has been or
will be placed on the original check.
• A replacement check for the original amount shall be issued at the next available
opportunity following verification. Checks are issued through the normal Town check -
issuance process and are subject to the same authorization requirements as original
checks.
• The Town Treasurer shall record the stop payment and reissuance in the Town’s
financial records to ensure accurate accounting of the transaction.
• The replacement check is subject to the same 180-day expiration period established by
this policy.
4. Unclaimed Funds
• Funds from checks that expire and are not claimed through a reissuance request shall be
treated as unclaimed property in accordance with Wisconsin’s Unclaimed Property Law,
Wis. Stat. Ch. 177.
• The Town Treasurer shall maintain a record of all expired and unclaimed checks and
shall report and remit unclaimed funds to the Wisconsin Department of Revenue as
required by Wis. Stat. Ch. 177.
5. Notice on Checks
• To the extent practicable, all Town-issued checks shall include the following notice
printed on their face: “VOID AFTER 180 DAYS.”
• The absence of this notice on a check does not extend the 180-day expiration period
established by this policy.

SECTION I – TITLE AND PURPOSE
The title of this ordinance is the Town of Winchester Driveway Ordinance. The purpose is to
regulate, for public health and safety reasons, the establishment, repair, construction,
improvement, modification, and reconstruction of private driveways, to assure that the
methods of repair, construction, improvement, modification, and reconstruction practices used
in any driveway will protect properly the public health, safety, and general welfare of persons in
the Town of Winchester.
SECTION II – AUTHORITY
The town board has the authority under the controlled access highway power granted pursuant
to ss. 66.0425, 83.027(10), 84.25(1) Wis. stats., to adopt a town driveway and highway access
ordinance and has the general authority under its village powers under ss. 60.10(2)(c), 60.22(3),
and 61.34(1) Wis. stats., to adopt this ordinance.
SECTION III – ADOPTION AND ABORGATION
A. This ordinance, adopted by a majority of the town board on a roll call vote with a quorum
present and voting and proper notice having been given, provides for the regulation by
Town Board of certain driveways and private roads and their access to public roadways in
the Town of Winchester.
B. This ordinance supersedes all prior Town of Winchester Driveway Ordinances. However,
where another ordinance imposes greater restriction, the provisions of the more restrictive
ordinance shall prevail.
SECTION IV – DEFINITIONS
A. “Driveway” means any private way, private road, or other avenue of private travel that runs
through any part of a private parcel of land that connects or will connect with any public
roadway, and will provide vehicular access from the public roadway to a residence,
business, recreational site, or other similarly appropriate use including temporary
driveways.
B. “Emergency Vehicle” means any fire, police, ambulance, or first responder vehicle used in
emergency of hazard activities in the town.
C. “Town” means the Town of Winchester, Vilas County, Wisconsin.
D. “Town Board” means the board of supervisors for the Town of Winchester, Vilas County,
Wisconsin, and includes any designee of the board authorized to act for the board.
E. “Town Clerk” means the clerk of the Town of Winchester, Vilas County, Wisconsin.
F. “permit” means the Town of Winchester Driveway Permit

TOWN OF WINCHESTER DRIVEWAY ORDIANCE
TOWN OF WINCHESTER, VILAS COUNTY WISCONSIN
G. “Wis. stats.” means the Wisconsin Statutes, including successor provisions to cited statutes.
SECTION V – COVERAGE
A. This ordinance applies to all driveways which occur or are proposed to occur in the Town of
Winchester, Vilas County, Wisconsin.
B. A private road providing access to more than 3 (three) residences will have separate
requirements found in the Town of Winchester Road Ordinance.
C. No person may establish or construct a driveway or reconstruct, reroute, or alter the
existing slope of any existing driveway without first obtaining a permit from the Town
Board.
D. Any person prior to and at the time of seeking a driveway permit must own or have legal
interest in and current legal access to the land to which the permit will apply.
E. Driveways accessing onto a County Highway must obtain approval from the proper
authority, Vilas County Zoning and Planning Department.
SECTION VI – SPECIFICATIONS
A. All work shall be performed without danger to or interference with traffic using a public
roadway.
B. Town road surfaces, slopes, shoulders, ditches, and vegetation disturbed by work on a
driveway shall be restored by the property owner.
C. All costs of installation and maintenance of culverts as well as public roadway restoration
shall be the sole responsibility of the property owner.
D. The edge of all driveways and private roads shall be located at least 15 (fifteen) feet from
the nearest side lot line except in the case of a driveway abutting a public road and
providing access to two adjacent parcels. Said driveway can be on the lot line or split
between parcels. A maintenance agreement and easement agreement must be recorded at
Vilas County Register of Deeds.
E. Driveways for a single property require:
1. A roadbed of 12 (twelve) feet in width
2. An unobstructed overhead clearance of 15 (fifteen) feet for ingress and egress
of Emergency Vehicles

F. Private roads for more than one property require:
1. A 66 (sixty-six) foot easement width, 33 (thirty-three) feet in each direction
from the center of the road
2. Graveling to a minimum width of 12 (twelve) feet with a minimum of 4 (four)
inches of compacted gravel over an appropriate base with sufficient drainage
3. Bridges to be inspected and rated to pass a 30 (thirty) ton fire apparatus safely
and to have a minimum width of 10 (ten) feet
4. A 50 (fifty) foot diameter turn around on all new or reconstructed private roads,
if space is not available for a 50 (fifty) foot diameter turn around, agreements
with adjacent landowners must be established to allow for the largest possible
turn to be built in the space available
5. An unobstructed overhead clearance of 15 (fifteen) feet for ingress and egress
of Emergency Vehicles
G. Unless otherwise stated, a minimum of 12 (twelve) inch diameter by 24 (twenty-four) foot
long culvert installed and maintained by the property owner under the proposed driveway
to provide proper drainage under the entrance and along the public roadway
1. Fill shall not cover the ends of the culvert
2. Both culvert ends shall be riprapped or sodded to prevent fill material from
spilling into the ditch and clogging the culvert
3. Work of placing culverts and riprap/sod shall proceed diligently and be
completed promptly after it is begun and shall present a neat appearance when
completed.
H. Entryways within 50 (fifty) feet of the centerline of any public roadway shall not exceed a
5% (five-percent) up or down slope. However, when existing property slopes exceed 10%
(ten-percent) the Town Board may allow entryway slope to be increased to minimize
grading damage to the property, but in no case shall entryways exceed 15% (fifteen-
percent) up or down slope and entryways exceeding 10% (ten-percent) shall provide
rounding at the intersection with the public road to prevent rear-end or mid-wheel dragging
to vehicles entering or leaving the property
I. Driveways should align with the public roadway at right angles to facilitate turning moves
from both directions and entryways should not be located adjacent to sharp vertical or
horizontal curves in the public roadway but shall be in positions where adequate stopping
sight is available to all vehicles.
J. Unless otherwise documented, the Town road right-of-way at the place of construction is
assumed to extend 33 (thirty-three) feet from the centerline of the Town road.
K. Permits for temporary driveways/roadways shall require the permit holder to return the
affected area to its natural state within 6 (six) months after use is halted.

TOWN OF WINCHESTER, VILAS COUNTY WISCONSIN
L. Construction of blacktop roads to town specification shall be completed prior to the Town
Board recommending approval of any land division
M. Prior to a transfer of a private road to the Town of Winchester the road must meet all the
requirements of a Town blacktopped/seal coated road.
N. All work shall be carried out to the satisfaction of the Town Board as to compliance with any
permits.
O. Failure to maintain driveways to the minimum standards listed in Section VI could result in
the inability of the Emergency Vehicles to provide prompt and effective emergency
response to private properties in the Town of Winchester.
SECTION VII – APPLICATION AND PERMIT PROVISIONS
A. An application for the Town of Winchester Driveway Permit is available from the Town Clerk
or on the Town website.
B. The permit applicant shall submit to the Town Clerk a completed application for each with
the appropriate fee and with the following attachments:
1. Sketch map: A rough sketch showing the conceptual area of the project and
approximate location and dimensions of the project. The sketch map may be
submitted to the Town Board prior to the submission of the other supporting
documents in order for the Town Board to provide initial comments and review of
the proposal. Formal approval for a permit will not be granted without the
submission of complete supporting documents.
2. The Town Board may require other documents to be attached to the application
including but not limited to: plat map, aerial photo/site analysis, soil/slope analysis,
construction plan.
C. The Town Board shall approve or deny every permit application and may, as a condition of
issuance, place specific restrictions or conditions on the permit, which shall require
compliance by the permittee.
D. Denial of permit
1. A denial of permit by the Town Board shall accompany an explanation of the facts
on which the permit has been denied.
2. The applicant may re-apply for the permit at any time after denial, but after two
consecutive denials on the same parcel another application may not be considered
for 60 (sixty) days.
E. The applicant shall notify the Town Board within 30 (thirty) days after completion of the
construction, reconstruction, rerouting, or alteration of the driveway/driveway access.
Within 30 days of notification the Town Board shall conduct an inspection of the driveway to
ensure full compliance with the permit and this ordinance.
ORDINANCE 2024-04

TOWN OF WINCHESTER, VILAS COUNTY WISCONSIN
F. Permits expire 1 (one) year after issuance and all approved construction must be completed
before the permit expires. Each permit may be renewed for a period of 6 (six) months, if
work is not completed by the end of the 6 (six) month renewal period, a new application
and fee must be submitted and approved.
G. Driveway permits will be valid for the original applicant and non-transferrable.
H. The applicant, his successor, or assignee agrees to hold harmless the Town of Winchester,
its agents and employees, against any action for personal injury or property damage
sustained by reason or exercise of this permit.
SECTION VIII – SEVERABILITY CLAUSE
If any provision of this ordinance or its application to any person or circumstance is held invalid,
the invalidity does not affect other provisions or applications of this ordinance that can be given
effect without the invalid provision or application, and to this end the provisions of this
ordinance are severable.
SECTION IX – EFFECTIVE DATE
This ordinance is effective on publication or posting.
The town clerk shall properly post/publish this ordinance as required under s. 60.80, Wis. stats.

Regular access period: Mondays, 10:00 AM – 1:00 PM
24-hour advance written or oral notice required to inspect or
copy records during this period. — Wis. Stat. § 19.34(2)(b)2.
Outside access period: contact clerk to schedule an

Electronic records available by email where practicable — no

COPY FEES
Fees shall not exceed the actual, necessary, and direct cost of

Fee schedule subject to adoption by Town Board and can be

Fees may be waived or reduced where the custodian

19.35(3)(e)
No fee for inspection that does not involve copying.
LIMITATIONS ON ACCESS
Access may be limited only where: (1) a state or federal
statute exempts the record; (2) a court has established a
common law limitation; or (3) the public interest in
withholding clearly outweighs the public interest in
disclosure. Any denial will be provided in writing with the
specific legal basis stated. — Wis. Stat. §§ 19.35–19.36
HOW TO SUBMIT A REQUEST
Requesters are not required to identify themselves or state the
purpose of a request. — Wis. Stat. § 19.35(1)(i)
• In person at Town Hall during access hours or by
appointment
• Email: clerk@winchester.wi.gov
• Mail: Town Clerk, 7228 CTH W, Winchester WI 54557
• Phone: 715-686-2123
• Online form at winchesterwi.com (encouraged, not required)
Note: While submission via the online form is not required, the
Clerk’s Office will generate an internal electronic request record
for tracking and recordkeeping purposes for every request received,
regardless of how it is submitted. Records will be delivered
electronically unless the requester specifies otherwise.
RESPONSE STANDARD
The custodian shall, as soon as practicable and without delay,
either fill the request or notify the requester of the determination
to deny, in whole or in part, and the reasons therefor. — Wis. Stat.
§ 19.35(4)(a)
Note: While 10 business days is not a statutory deadline, the
Clerk’s Office will make every best effort to respond within that
timeframe. If a request cannot be fulfilled within 10 business days,
the requester will be notified with an explanation and an estimated
completion date.
Records may not be destroyed after a request is received until the
request is fulfilled, or at least 60 days after denial. — Wis. Stat. §
19.35(5)
REMEDIES FOR WRONGFUL DENIAL
A requester who believes access has been wrongfully denied may:
(1) bring a mandamus action in circuit court; or (2) request the
District Attorney or Attorney General to bring such action. —
Wis. Stat. § 19.37(1)
If the requester prevails, the court shall award reasonable attorney
fees, damages of not less than $100, and other actual costs. — Wis.
Stat. § 19.37(2)(a)

ORDINANCE NO. 2026-07
ORDINANCE TO APPOINT ALTERNATE MEMBER FOR THE BOARD
OF REVIEW — YEAR 2026 PROCEEDINGS
SECTION I – PURPOSE
To provide for the appointment of an alternate member to serve on the Town of Winchester
Board of Review in the event a standing member is removed from consideration of an
individual case, or is otherwise unable to serve, during the Year 2026 Board of Review
proceedings.
SECTION II – AUTHORITY
The Town Board is authorized to provide for the appointment of alternate members to the
town board of review as follows:
A. General town board authority: § 60.22(1), Wis. Stats.
B. Wis. Stat. §§ 70.46(1) and 70.47(6m)(c), authorizing the town board to provide for the
appointment of alternate members to serve on the board of review when a standing
member is removed under Wis. Stat. § 70.47(6m)(a) or (b), or is otherwise unable to
serve.

SECTION III – APPOINTMENT OF ALTERNATE MEMBER
Pursuant to the authority cited in Section II, the Town Board hereby provides for the
appointment of an alternate to serve on the Town of Winchester Board of Review for the Year
2026 Board of Review proceedings, as follows:
A. The following elector of the Town of Winchester is hereby named as alternate, to serve in
the order indicated, in the event a standing member of the Board of Review is removed
under Wis. Stat. § 70.47(6m)(a) or (b), or is otherwise unable to serve:
1. Alternate 1: Joseph Discianno
B. The Town Clerk shall maintain a public record of this appointment and shall notify the
named alternate in the event a standing member of the Board of Review is removed or
unable to serve.
C. This appointment is effective for the Year 2026 Board of Review proceedings only and
does not extend beyond that year absent further action of the Town Board.
SECTION IV – SEVERABILITY
Should any section, clause, or provision of this ordinance be declared invalid by a court of
competent jurisdiction, such invalidity shall not affect the validity of the ordinance as a whole
or any part thereof other than the part so declared to be invalid.
SECTION V – EFFECTIVE DATE
This ordinance shall be effective for the Year 2026 Board of Review proceedings upon passage
by the Town Board of Winchester and posting/publication as required by Wis. Stat. § 60.80.
The Town Clerk shall properly post and/or publish this ordinance as required under Wis. Stat.
§ 60.80.

roll call vote with a quorum present and voting, on the 14 day of September, 2026.

SUBJECT: Absentee Ballot Return Best Practices
1. Summary
On July 9, 2026, the Commission unanimously approved the publication of guidance for voters to help them
understand when, where, and how to return an absentee ballot. The attached guidance will be made available to
media and posted on the Commission website. Clerks may wish to use the guidance in their own materials for
voters or to help train staff. No action is required of clerks.
2. Questions
Questions regarding the attached absentee ballot return guidance can be directed to elections@wi.gov or 608-
261-2028.
Published 7/17/2026
Absentee Ballot Return : Best Practices
Introduction
In Wisconsin, any voter can choose to cast their ballot one of three ways:
a. At their polling location on Election Day
b. Absentee ballot returned: (1) by mail, (2) by delivery to a clerk’s office, or
(3) depositing in a drop box
c. In-person absentee ballot (sometimes called early voting) at an officially
designated site beginning two weeks before Election Day
1. Voting Absentee
Do I need a reason to vote absentee?
No, you do not need a reason or excuse to vote by absentee ballot in Wisconsin. Any
Wisconsin voter who wishes to vote absentee may do so by submitting a request as
described below.
How do I vote absentee?
There are three ways to request an absentee ballot.
1. Online. In just a few simple steps, you can officially request your absentee
ballot online at MyVote.wi.gov, which will generate an email notification to
your municipal clerk.
2. By Mail. If you are a registered Wisconsin voter, you can download
the Application For Absentee Ballot. Then, fill out the form and mail it to your
municipal clerk’s office. With few exceptions (e.g., you are indefinitely
confined, live permanently overseas), you must also include a copy of your
acceptable photo ID with your absentee ballot request. Information on the
Photo ID needed to vote in Wisconsin is available at BringIt.wi.gov.
3. By Email or Fax. You can also request an absentee ballot by carefully
composing and sending an email or fax to your municipal clerk that includes:
• Your full name;
• Voting address;
Published 7/17/2026
• Mailing address;
• The election in which you are voting;
• A copy of your photo ID (if you have not provided it with a previous
absentee ballot request).
Your clerk must receive your absentee ballot request no later than 5 p.m. on the
Thursday before Election Day. However, we recommend making this request as soon
as possible, so you have time to receive, complete, and return your ballot to be
counted.
Note: Before your clerk can send you an absentee ballot, you must be registered to
vote. Find out if you’re registered at MyVote.WI.gov. Select “Register to vote,” and enter
your name and date of birth.
2. Returning an Absentee Ballot
There are three ways to return your absentee ballot:
• By Mail
• Using a drop box
• Directly to your clerk’s office
When should I return my completed absentee ballot by mail?
Mail transit times vary. Do not delay returning your completed absentee ballot. If a
mailed ballot arrives after 8 p.m. on Election Day, it will not be counted.1
The Wisconsin Elections Commission recommends putting your ballot in the mail at
least 10 days before Election Day to ensure it is received in time. Voters who are out-of-
state may need more time to ensure timely return. If you return your absentee ballot
through the mail the week before Election Day, there is a significant risk that your ballot
may not be received and counted.
Your returned ballot must be sent to your city, village, or town clerk. This means:
• Do not mail or deliver the ballot to your county clerk.
1 In Wisconsin, it does not matter when your ballot is postmarked. Some other states use the postmark to
determine if a ballot can be counted. Wisconsin does not use the postmark. In Wisconsin, absentee ballots
must arrive before polls close on Election Day to be counted.
Published 7/17/2026
• Do not mail or deliver the ballot to the Wisconsin Elections Commission.
• Do not mail or deliver the ballot to the Wisconsin Secretary of State.
• Do not mail or deliver the ballot to the courthouse. The clerk of court is not your
municipal clerk.
Concerned your ballot will not arrive on-time through the mail?
You can also hand-deliver your absentee ballot directly to your municipal
clerk. On Election Day, you may hand-deliver your absentee ballot to your
polling place or central counting facility (if applicable).2 Or, if your clerk has
established drop boxes for absentee ballot return, you may return the ballot
using a drop box.
NOTE: You cannot return someone else’s ballot unless you are assisting a
voter with a disability.
When should I return my completed absentee ballot by drop box?
When a drop box is available for use is determined by each municipality. Some
municipalities allow the drop boxes to be used on Election Day and some do not.
Those available on Election Day usually have a time cut-off after which the drop box
cannot be used. It is recommended that a voter only use a drop box prior to Election
Day. If on Election Day, contact your clerk to determine if a drop box is available.
When should I return my completed absentee ballot directly to my clerk?
You may return your absentee ballot directly to your clerk prior to Election Day. If you
are concerned your absentee ballot will not arrive by Election Day, you must deliver
your absentee ballot to your clerk. On Election Day, you must return your ballot to your
polling place or central counting facility (if applicable).2
2 Most Wisconsin cities, villages, and towns count absentee ballots at the polling place. Some jurisdictions
(mostly larger cities) count absentee ballots at a central counting facility. Contact your municipal clerk to
determine where your ballot will be counted.
Published 7/17/2026
3. Checking on Your Ballot
Has my ballot arrived on time?
First, check your absentee ballot status online at MyVote.wi.gov by selecting “Track My
Ballot”. If the website does not show your ballot returned, you can also call your
municipal clerk.
If I received an absentee ballot, but did not return it, can I still vote at the
polls on Election Day?
Yes. As long as you do not return your absentee ballot, you can still vote at the polls.
Once an absentee ballot has been returned to the municipal clerk, it cannot be spoiled
and reissued for any reason.
If I returned my completed ballot in the mail, can I change my mind and
vote in person on Election Day?
No.
If you return your ballot in the mail, you cannot vote in person on Election
Day, even if the absentee ballot has not arrived.
What if I am a military or overseas voter?
The Federal Voting Assistance Program (FVAP) provides detailed recommendations for
absent military and overseas voters.
• Military voters at sea or at overseas facilities without access to the military postal
system should return their ballot at least 35 calendar days before the election.
• Military voters with access to the military postal system and civilian voters
overseas should return their ballot at least 30 calendar days before the election.
• Stateside (CONUS) military voters and eligible family members should return
their ballot at least 11 calendar days before the election.
In all cases, FVAP recommends that military and overseas voters complete and return
the ballot as soon as it is received.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: FOR MORE INFORMATION, CONTACT:
July 21, 2026 Emilee Miklas, emilee.miklas@wisconsin.gov
Don’t Bet on Your Ballot: WEC Warns Voters Against
Election Gambling
MADISON – With predication markets and online gambling platforms growing in popularity, the
Wisconsin Elections Commission is warning voters: if you bet on an election - it could cost you your vote.
“We want voters to understand that they cannot legally make a bet on an election and cast a ballot in that
same election,” WEC Administrator Meagan Wolfe said. “We are not able to police someone placing a bet
on these platforms, but it’s important for voters to understand the consequences if they bet on an election
outcome.”
Wisconsin law is clear: a voter cannot, even indirectly, make a bet or wager on the outcome of an election
and then vote in that same election:
• Wisconsin Statute § 6.03(2) explicitly disqualifies electors from voting “in any election in which
the person has made or become interested, directly or indirectly, in any bet or wager depending upon
the result of the election.”
• Wisconsin Statute § 12.13(1)(a) makes it a Class I felony to intentionally vote in an election
without being qualified to do so.
Voters who place bets on elections and then try to vote in that election may be subject to voter qualification
administrative challenges, which, if successful, would prevent them from being able to cast their ballot and
could also result in a referral to the District Attorney.
Earlier this month, the bipartisan Commission unanimously voted and approved a memo during its July 9,
2026, meeting outlining legal ramifications and concerns about prediction markets and elections. You can
view the memo in the open session materials here (beginning on page 149).
Prediction markets, most prominently run by the companies Kalshi and Polymarket, have quickly emerged
and become popular across the United States. Users can trade and invest in “yes” or “no” outcomes, from
sporting events to what the President may do on a certain day.
Regulation of prediction markets has been a recent litigation topic at the state and federal levels.
There are currently no federal laws addressing prediction markets for elections, however the Stop Trading
On Predictions (STOP) Corrupt Bets Act of 2026 (H.R. 8123) which would ban prediction market bets on
elections has been introduced as a bill. The U.S. Senate also has banned its members and staff from
prediction market betting.
More than half of states (23) have laws that prohibit betting or wagering on elections, at least under certain
circumstances, according to a Pew Research Center analysis of data from the National Conference of State
Legislatures (NCSL).
Additionally, Governor Tony Evers signed Executive Order #294 to address the growing concern for
government officials’ use of prediction markets, which prohibits all Wisconsin state executive branch
employees from “disclosing or using any nonpublic information obtained due to their public service to
personally profit from, avoid loss from, or assist another person or entity, including spouses and family
members, in profiting or avoiding loss from participating in prediction markets.”

August 11, 2026
Office of the Vilas County Clerk
To the voters of Vilas County
Notice is hereby given of a Partisan Primary election to be held in Vilas County on August 11, 2026, at
which the nominees for the offices named below shall be chosen. The names of the candidates for each
office, whose nominations have been certified to or filed in this office, are given under the title of the office,
under the appropriate party, each in its proper column, together with the questions submitted to a vote, if
any, in the sample ballot below.
Information to Voters
Upon entering the polling place and before being permitted to vote, a voter shall:
• state their name and address
• show an acceptable form of photo identification*
• sign the poll book**
*If a voter does not have acceptable photo identification, the voter may obtain a free photo ID for
voting from the Division of Motor Vehicles.
**If the voter is unable to sign the poll book due to disability, a poll worker may write the word
“exempt.”
If a voter is not registered to vote, they may register to vote at the polling place serving their residence if
the voter provides proof of residence.
Where ballots are distributed to voters, the initials of two inspectors must appear on the ballot.
Upon being permitted to vote, the voter shall enter a voting booth or go to a machine and cast their
ballot. The vote should not be cast in any manner other than specified here. Sample ballots or other
materials to assist the voter in marking their ballot may be taken into the booth and copied. The sample
ballot shall not be shown to anyone so as to reveal how the ballot is marked.
A voter who is a parent or guardian may be accompanied by the voter's minor child or minor ward.
An election official may inform the voter of the proper manner for casting a vote but the official may not
advise or indicate a particular voting choice.
Assistance for Voting
A voter may select an individual to assist in casting their vote if the voter declares to the presiding
official that they are unable to read, have difficulty reading, writing, or understanding English, or that
due to disability are unable to cast their ballot. The selected individual rendering assistance may not be
the voter's employer or an agent of that employer or an officer or agent of a labor organization which
represents the voter. If a voter is unable to state their name and address, an assistant may also do so
for the voter.
At the partisan primary, the voter shall select the party of their choice. Voting for candidates of
more than one party may invalidate the ballot. The voter must cast a vote for individual candidates.
Where Optical Scan Voting is used
• If a party preference is designated, and votes are cast for ballot candidates of another
party or write-in votes are cast in another party, only votes cast in the designated party
will count.
• If a party preference is not designated, and votes are cast for candidates (or write-in
votes are cast) in more than one party, no votes will be counted
Within the party of their choice, the voter shall fill in the oval or connect the arrow next to the name of
the candidate of their choice for each office for which they intend to vote. To vote for a person whose
name does not appear on the ballot, the voter shall write in the name of the person of their choice in the
space provided for a write-in vote and fill in the oval or connect the arrow next to the write-in line. On
referendum questions, the voter shall fill in the oval or connect the arrow next to "yes" if in favor of the
question, or the voter shall fill in the oval or connect the arrow next to "no" if opposed to the question.
Spoiled Ballots
If a voter spoils an optical scan ballot, they shall return it to an election official who shall issue another
ballot in its place, but not more than three ballots shall be issued to any one voter. If the ballot has
not been initialed by two inspectors or is defective in any other way, the voter shall return it to the
election official, who shall issue a proper ballot in its place.
After Voting the Ballot
After an official optical scan ballot is marked, it may be inserted in the security sleeve, so the
marks do not show. The voter shall insert the ballot in the voting device and discard the sleeve or
deliver the ballot to an inspector for deposit. If a central count system is used, the voter shall
insert the ballot in the ballot box and discard the sleeve or deliver the ballot to an inspector for
deposit. The voter shall leave the polling place promptly.

FROM: Staff Counsel
SUBJECT: Prediction Markets and Wisconsin Elections
1. Introduction
Prediction markets, most prominently run by the companies Kalshi and Polymarket, have quickly emerged
and become popular. A person can “buy” shares of a prediction concerning an ou tcome, and if correct
receive money in return, and if incorrect, lose the money offered. This memo concerns prediction markets
and elections. While a person may make a bet on many different outcomes, elections are a prominent item
on prediction markets, which raises serious but not well-known concerns about voting in Wisconsin. This
memo provides to the Commission a general introdu ction to prediction markets, the current legal
landscape of prediction markets and elections, and a recommendation to direct staff to issue a press release
on election betting to provide information to Wisc onsin voters who may not know that they cannot both
make a bet on an election and also vote in that election.
Prediction Markets
A prediction market is an online platform that allows users to trade and invest in real-world “Yes” or “No”
outcomes, from sporting events to what the President will say on a given day.1 They function similarly to
a stock exchange, but users can only buy binary contracts (yes/no) on whether a specific event will occur
or not.2 Users purchase shares of “Yes” if they believe an event will happen or “No” if they believe it will
not.3 If they are correct, a trader receives the full contract value of $1.4 If a trader is wrong, the contract’s
value becomes worthless ($0). 5 Shares are priced depending on the odds of an event occurring and

2 US election betting boom to test prediction markets’ insider trading controls, https://www.msn.com/en-us/money/news/us-

fluctuate until the outcome is fully resolv ed, reflecting traders’ collective beliefs. 6 For example, if the
shares of “Yes” are priced at 84 cents, this implies that there is an 84% chance of the event occurring.
These trades include elections.7 Some of the highest volume political markets on Kalshi include who will
be the 2028 Democratic and Republi can nominees for president and w ho will win the 2028 presidential
election.8 Platforms Kalshi and Polymarket have surged in popularity since the 2024 election.9
Prediction markets are regulated by the Commodi ty Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), which
federally regulates financial derivatives. 10 The most prominent prediction market platform, Kalshi, is
registered with the CFTC as a Designated Contract Market (DCM).11 Polymarket has recently launched a
U.S. operation, with the CFTC approving its plan to return as a regulated, intermediated trading platform.12
However, its main exchange is not U.S.-regulate d, has not generally mandate d “Know Your Customer”
identity checks, and while it bars U.S. residents, those controls are easily bypassed, such as with a VPN.13
“Know Your Customer” identity checks require regul ated businesses and professionals to verify the
identity, suitability, and risks of maintaining a business relationship with a customer.14
Current State of the Law
Regulation of prediction markets has been a recent litigation topic at the state and federal levels.15 Some
states—which have the authority to regulate gamb ling—believe that they s hould regulate prediction
markets, as they are equivalent to gambling. 16 However, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission
believes it should regulate predic tion markets under the special rule of the Commodity Exchange Act
(CEA), which allows the CFTC to review and potentially ban certain event contracts deemed contrary to
the public interest. 7 U.S.C. §§ 7a-2(c)(5)(C)(i)(I), (V). 17 The CFTC regulates event contracts to ensure
that trades are done on DCMs and comply with the CEA. 18 The CTFC can only exercise its authority if
the contracts involve particular acti vities enumerated in the CEA including activities th at are unlawful
activity under any Federal or State law, terrorism, assassination, war, gaming, or other similar activities

contrary to the public interest.19 The issue of who gets to regulate election contracts in prediction markets
comes down to whether or not they are “gaming” under the special rule of the CEA or involve unlawful
activity under State law.20
In 2024, the CFTC attempted to exercise its authority under the CEA by prohibiting Kalshi from offering
“congressional control contracts” on which party would take control of Congress in the midterm election.
KalshiEX LLC v. Commodity Futures Trading Comm’n , No. CV 23-3257 (JMC), 2024 WL 4164694
(D.D.C. Sept. 12, 2024), dismissed, No. 24-5205, 2025 WL 1349979 (D.C. Cir. May 7, 2025). Kalshi filed
suit challenging the CFTC’s order as arbitrary, capricious, and contrary to law under the Administrative
Procedure Act. 5 U.S.C. § 706. Id. at 1. The DC District Court judge granted summary judgement for
Kalshi, holding that elections are not games so “congressional control contracts” are not “gaming” by its
“ordinary, plain meaning” and therefore do not fall under the CFTC’s mandate. Id.at 7.
In Wisconsin, Wis. Stat. § 6.03(2) disqualifies elect ors from voting “in any election in which the person
has made or become interested, directly or indirectly, in any bet or wager depending upon the result of the
election.” See also, Wis. Stats. §§ 6.87(2) (absentee vot er certification of qualifications) 6.94 and
7.52(5)(b) (challenged elector oath), and, especially, 12.13 (creating a cl ass I felony for “vot[ing] at any
election or meeting if that pers on does not have the necessary elect or qualifications and residence
requirements”). Wisconsin Stat. § 945.01(1) defines “Bet” as “a bargain in which the parties agree that,
dependent upon chance even though accompanied by some skill, one stands to win or lose something of
value specified in the agreement.”
Additionally, Governor Tony Evers signed Executive Order #294 to address the growing concern for
government officials’ use of pred iction markets, which prohibits a ll Wisconsin state executive branch
employees from “disclosing or using any nonpublic in formation obtained due to their public service to
personally profit from, avoi d loss from, or assist a nother person or entity, in cluding spouses and family
members, in profiting or avoiding loss from participating in prediction markets.” Wisconsin also has laws
against insider trading in general. See, Wis. Stat. § 611.31.
There are currently no federal laws addressing prediction markets for elections, however the Stop
Trading On Predictions (STOP) Corrupt Bets Act of 2026 (H.R. 8123) which would ban prediction market
bets on elections has been introduced as a bill. The U.S. Senate has also banned its members and staff
from prediction market betting.
3. Discussion
Commission staff believe that the increasing prevalen ce of prediction markets raises the possibility that
Wisconsin electors may attempt to place a bet or wage r on an election and then vote in that election in
violation of Wis. Stat. § 6.03(2).
Wisconsin faces a similar challenge as the CEA in Kalshi EX LLC v. CFTC in determining whether placing
trades on an election-related prediction market qualifies as “any bet or wager,” which would disqualify an
elector from voting in that election. Commission staff believe the prohibition against “any bet or wager
depending upon the result of the election” § 6.03(2) includes making trades on election-related prediction

https://www.findlaw.com/legalblogs/federal-courts/are-politics-about-to-get-even-more-corrupt-federal-judge-allows-
gambling-on-elections/ (last visited June 24, 2026).
20 Id.

7/9/2026
markets.“[A]ny bet or wager” is all-encompassing la nguage that suggests prediction markets would be
included in this prohibition, preventing an elector from voting who has placed a bid on an election-related
prediction market. At the very least staff do not see how an elector coul d, in the context of a challenge,
truthfully say that they “have not made any bet or wager or become directly or indirectly interested in any
bet or wager depending upon the result of this election” if they have offered money in a prediction market,
and would receive money if they are correct and lose money if they are incorrect.
Despite the ongoing legal disagreeme nts on whether prediction markets are “bets,” Wisconsin law is
relatively clear that an elector cannot, even indir ectly, both make a bet or wager on the outcome of an
election and then vote in that same election. It is also increasingly easy to participate in such predictions,
and the prominence of these markets is likely far greater than knowledge about Wis. Stat. § 6.03(2). Staff
are not here concerned with the legality of placing a bet on an election in general, but believe that electors
should know that if they do place such a bet, Wis. Stat. § 6.03(2) likely prohibits them from voting and
that Wis. Stat. § 12.13(1)(a) makes it a class I felony to vote without being qualified to do so.
4. Conclusion
Commission staff believe that predication market betting on elections is likely to become more prevalent
in Wisconsin. With the lack of clarity and legal consensus concerning whether prediction markets qualify
as gaming or betting, many Wisconsinites may not understand using predic tion markets as betting at all,
or that such actions prevent th em from voting under Wis. Stat. § 6 .03(2) subject to felony-level
consequences. Staff recommend that the Commission direct staff to issue a press release that raises
awareness about this issue.

Postmark Definition
• August 12, 2025 –Proposed rule filed in the Federal Register – Comment Period ended on 9/11/2025
• November 24, 2025 – Final Rule published in Federal Register
• December 24, 2025 – Final Rule effective in the Domestic Mail Manual (DMM)
• Addition to the Domestic Mail Manual (DMM) add Section 608.11 “Postmarks and Postal Possession.”
• This Section identifies the types of Postal Service markings that qualify as postmarks and describes
the circumstances under which those markings are applied. It also advises customers of how to
obtain evidence of the date on which the Postal Service accepts possession of their mailings.
• This new language in the DMM does not change any existing postal operations or postmarking
practices but is instead intended to improve public understanding of postmarks and their relationship
to the date of mailing.

Postmarking Myths and Facts
MYTH: The Postal Service has changed the way postmarks are applied to mailpieces
FACT: The Postal Service has not changed and is not changing our postmarking practices, which
have been consistent since we began moving away from hand-canceling every item at Post Offices
decades ago.
MYTH: The Postal Service has long offered the postmark as a way of proving when mail was sent
FACT: Customers have used postmarking for their own purposes, but postmarking is not and has
not been a service that the Postal Service has provided to the public for such purposes. The
postmark has always fundamentally existed to perform functions (including cancelation of postage)
internal to Postal Service operations.

Postmarking Myths and Facts
MYTH: The Postal Service didn’t notify the public about this update to its language
FACT: The Postal Service engaged in discussions with customer groups, posted information on our
website, and initiated a public notice and comment period in the Federal Register in August 2025,
which concluded when the Postal Service published its final notice on this topic, including responses
to the comments received, in November 2025.
MYTH: Postmarks show when and where the Postal Service took possession of my mail
FACT: A postmark date does not necessarily indicate the first day that the Postal Service took
possession of the mailpiece. Rather, it confirms that the Postal Service accepted custody of a
mailpiece, and that the mailpiece was in the possession of the Postal Service on the identified date.

SUBJECT: USPS Rule Update
1. Introduction
The purpose of this memo is to update clerks on a recent decision in the California et al. v. USPS
litigation regarding the United States Postal Service’s new rule regarding new requirements for mailing
absentee ballots for federal elections.
On August 27, 2026, a U.S. District Court Judge issued a temporary restraining order. This order stays
implementation or enforcement of certain sections of the United States Postal Service’s rule for 14
days.
2. What is the impact of this decision on Wisconsin?
The temporary restraining order preserves the status quo. This means Wisconsin election officials are
not required to comply with the new requirements of the USPS rule at this time and can proceed to
issue and mail absentee ballots normally.
3. Will there be any further action on this case before the General Election?
Yes. A hearing is scheduled for September 3, 2026, and additional proceedings and/or appeals may
occur before the General Election . The Commission will provide further information as the case
develops.
4. Questions?
Please see the attached FAQ document for more detailed information regarding the rule and injunction.
You may direct any further questions to our Help Desk at elections@wi.gov or (608) 261-2028.

SUBJECT: Frequently Asked Questions: USPS By Mail Voting Rule
Q 1: What is the new USPS by mail voting rule, and how does it impact Wisconsin?
A: In March 2026, President Trump issued an Executive Order directing USPS to develop an
administrative rule that would regulate federal absentee voting by mail. USPS finalized and published
that rule on Wednesday, August 26, 2026. The rule applies nationwide to any state that uses the USPS to
send or receive absentee ballots.
The rule proposed a system where all states would use a specific ballot envelope containing personalized
barcodes for absentee voters. States would have to individually upload voter information for each by
mail absentee voter (except military and overseas voters) into a USPS absentee voter portal prior to
sending the absentee ballots out. Then, USPS would scan the barcodes on the envelopes to determine if
the ballot can or cannot be delivered to the voter by USPS. Under the rule, which is now blocked by a
federal court, USPS would not deliver any absentee ballots it could not verify through its portal.
You can read the full text of the rule here: https://public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2026-17238.pdf
USPS has also developed an FAQ for its rule that it issued before the rule was blocked. You can read
that here, but please note it contains outdated information and the provisions of the rule described are
not currently in effect: https://about.usps.com/what/government-services/election-mail/pdf/faq-usps-
final-rule-ballot-mail-federal-elections.pdf
Q
2: Is the USPS rule currently in effect?
A: No. On Thursday, August 27, a federal court entered an order blocking the rule, and USPS is
currently unable to enforce it or compel states to comply with it.

Q 3: What did the court do?
A: The federal court blocked all mandatory components of the USPS rule. The court said that while
USPS could continue to build the portal and develop these systems, no state can be compelled to use
them.
Q 4: Can USPS refuse to deliver absentee ballots if states don’t follow the rule?
A: No. Because enforcement of the rule is currently blocked by a federal court, USPS must continue to
mail absentee ballots as usual.
Q 5: Will Wisconsin comply with the rule even if it's not in effect?
A: No. Wisconsin cannot comply for several reasons. First, the USPS portal does not exist. USPS has
given no indication of when or whether it will exist, and USPS has provided no training on how the
portal will be used. The USPS rule is not a simple administrative change. It proposes a brand-new,
highly complex, untested system involving new carrier envelope design, information coded into
Intelligent Mail barcodes, a USPS-run database of voter information (input by clerks), none of which the
Commission or clerks have been trained to develop or use. The USPS rule was developed and
published in under five months, and USPS has not issued any training or explanation of how this system
will actually work.
Second, the first batches of absentee ballots for the November election will be going out across the
country starting the week of August 31, including in Wisconsin. It is too late for Wisconsin, or any state,
to make significant changes to election law, policy, or procedure because voting is underway.
Finally, state and federal caselaw prohibit Wisconsin from making major changes in close proximity
to an ongoing election. Purcell v. Gonzalez, 549 U.S. 1 (2006); Hawkins v. Wisconsin Elections
Commission, 2020 WI 75, 393 Wis. 2d 629, 948 N.W.2d 877.
Q 6: What will happen next? Will anything change before the November election?
A: Likely not. The rule has been blocked while the litigation continues, and the judge that blocked the
rule reasoned that the states challenging will likely be successful in arguing that the rule violates the law.
While it’s possible that an appeals court could disagree with the federal judge who blocked the rule, the
likelihood that any court will allow the rule to go back into effect lessens as we get closer to Election
Day. This is because federal courts in particular, including the U.S. Supreme Court, are usually reluctant
to change the rules for voting and procedure in close proximity to an election.
Nothing is guaranteed, but the Commission will provide timely updates if something changes.

VOTING BY ABSENTEE BALLOT
Any qualified elector who is unable or unwilling to appear at the polling place on Election Day may submit a request to vote an absentee ballot to their municipal clerk. A qualified elector is any U.S. citizen, who will be 18 years of age or older on Election Day, who has resided in the ward or municipality where he or she wishes to vote for at least 28 consecutive days before the election. The elector must also be registered in order to receive an absentee ballot. Proof of identification must be provided before an absentee ballot may be issued.
You must make a request for an absentee ballot in writing or online at MyVote.wi.gov.
Contact your municipal clerk and request that an application for an absentee ballot be sent to you for the primary or election or both. You may also submit a written request in the form of a letter or you may apply for an absentee ballot online at MyVote.wi.gov. Your written request must list your voting address within the municipality where you wish to vote, the address where the absentee ballot should be sent, if different, and your signature. You may make application to your municipal clerk for an absentee ballot in person, by mail, by fax, by email or at MyVote.wi.gov.
Making application to receive an absentee ballot by mail

Voting an absentee ballot in person
You may also request and vote an absentee ballot in the clerk's office or other specified location during the days and hours specified for casting an absentee ballot in person.

Absentee Ballot Return : Best Practices
Introduction
In Wisconsin, any voter can choose to cast their ballot one of three ways:
a. At their polling location on Election Day
b. Absentee ballot returned: (1) by mail, (2) by delivery to a clerk’s office, or
(3) depositing in a drop box
c. In-person absentee ballot (sometimes called early voting) at an officially
designated site beginning two weeks before Election Day
1. Voting Absentee
Do I need a reason to vote absentee?
No, you do not need a reason or excuse to vote by absentee ballot in Wisconsin. Any
Wisconsin voter who wishes to vote absentee may do so by submitting a request as
described below.
How do I vote absentee?
There are three ways to request an absentee ballot.
1. Online. In just a few simple steps, you can officially request your absentee
ballot online at MyVote.wi.gov, which will generate an email notification to
your municipal clerk.
2. By Mail. If you are a registered Wisconsin voter, you can download
the Application For Absentee Ballot. Then, fill out the form and mail it to your
municipal clerk’s office. With few exceptions (e.g., you are indefinitely
confined, live permanently overseas), you must also include a copy of your
acceptable photo ID with your absentee ballot request. Information on the
Photo ID needed to vote in Wisconsin is available at BringIt.wi.gov.
3. By Email or Fax. You can also request an absentee ballot by carefully
composing and sending an email or fax to your municipal clerk that includes:
• Your full name;
• Voting address;
Published 7/17/2026
• Mailing address;
• The election in which you are voting;
• A copy of your photo ID (if you have not provided it with a previous
absentee ballot request).
Your clerk must receive your absentee ballot request no later than 5 p.m. on the
Thursday before Election Day. However, we recommend making this request as soon
as possible, so you have time to receive, complete, and return your ballot to be
counted.
Note: Before your clerk can send you an absentee ballot, you must be registered to
vote. Find out if you’re registered at MyVote.WI.gov. Select “Register to vote,” and enter
your name and date of birth.
2. Returning an Absentee Ballot
There are three ways to return your absentee ballot:
• By Mail
• Using a drop box
• Directly to your clerk’s office
When should I return my completed absentee ballot by mail?
Mail transit times vary. Do not delay returning your completed absentee ballot. If a
mailed ballot arrives after 8 p.m. on Election Day, it will not be counted.1
The Wisconsin Elections Commission recommends putting your ballot in the mail at
least 10 days before Election Day to ensure it is received in time. Voters who are out-of-
state may need more time to ensure timely return. If you return your absentee ballot
through the mail the week before Election Day, there is a significant risk that your ballot
may not be received and counted.
Your returned ballot must be sent to your city, village, or town clerk. This means:
• Do not mail or deliver the ballot to your county clerk.
1 In Wisconsin, it does not matter when your ballot is postmarked. Some other states use the postmark to
determine if a ballot can be counted. Wisconsin does not use the postmark. In Wisconsin, absentee ballots
must arrive before polls close on Election Day to be counted.
Published 7/17/2026
• Do not mail or deliver the ballot to the Wisconsin Elections Commission.
• Do not mail or deliver the ballot to the Wisconsin Secretary of State.
• Do not mail or deliver the ballot to the courthouse. The clerk of court is not your
municipal clerk.
Concerned your ballot will not arrive on-time through the mail?
You can also hand-deliver your absentee ballot directly to your municipal
clerk. On Election Day, you may hand-deliver your absentee ballot to your
polling place or central counting facility (if applicable).2 Or, if your clerk has
established drop boxes for absentee ballot return, you may return the ballot
using a drop box.
NOTE: You cannot return someone else’s ballot unless you are assisting a
voter with a disability.
When should I return my completed absentee ballot by drop box?
When a drop box is available for use is determined by each municipality. Some
municipalities allow the drop boxes to be used on Election Day and some do not.
Those available on Election Day usually have a time cut-off after which the drop box
cannot be used. It is recommended that a voter only use a drop box prior to Election
Day. If on Election Day, contact your clerk to determine if a drop box is available.
When should I return my completed absentee ballot directly to my clerk?
You may return your absentee ballot directly to your clerk prior to Election Day. If you
are concerned your absentee ballot will not arrive by Election Day, you must deliver
your absentee ballot to your clerk. On Election Day, you must return your ballot to your
polling place or central counting facility (if applicable).2
2 Most Wisconsin cities, villages, and towns count absentee ballots at the polling place. Some jurisdictions
(mostly larger cities) count absentee ballots at a central counting facility. Contact your municipal clerk to
determine where your ballot will be counted.
Published 7/17/2026
3. Checking on Your Ballot
Has my ballot arrived on time?
First, check your absentee ballot status online at MyVote.wi.gov by selecting “Track My
Ballot”. If the website does not show your ballot returned, you can also call your
municipal clerk.
If I received an absentee ballot, but did not return it, can I still vote at the
polls on Election Day?
Yes. As long as you do not return your absentee ballot, you can still vote at the polls.
Once an absentee ballot has been returned to the municipal clerk, it cannot be spoiled
and reissued for any reason.
If I returned my completed ballot in the mail, can I change my mind and
vote in person on Election Day?
No.
If you return your ballot in the mail, you cannot vote in person on Election
Day, even if the absentee ballot has not arrived.
What if I am a military or overseas voter?
The Federal Voting Assistance Program (FVAP) provides detailed recommendations for
absent military and overseas voters.
• Military voters at sea or at overseas facilities without access to the military postal
system should return their ballot at least 35 calendar days before the election.
• Military voters with access to the military postal system and civilian voters
overseas should return their ballot at least 30 calendar days before the election.
• Stateside (CONUS) military voters and eligible family members should return
their ballot at least 11 calendar days before the election.
In all cases, FVAP recommends that military and overseas voters complete and return
the ballot as soon as it is received.

Postmarking Myths and Facts
MYTH: The Postal Service has changed the way postmarks are applied to mailpieces
FACT: The Postal Service has not changed and is not changing our postmarking practices, which
have been consistent since we began moving away from hand-canceling every item at Post Offices
decades ago.
MYTH: The Postal Service has long offered the postmark as a way of proving when mail was sent
FACT: Customers have used postmarking for their own purposes, but postmarking is not and has
not been a service that the Postal Service has provided to the public for such purposes. The
postmark has always fundamentally existed to perform functions (including cancelation of postage)
internal to Postal Service operations.

Postmarking Myths and Facts
MYTH: The Postal Service didn’t notify the public about this update to its language
FACT: The Postal Service engaged in discussions with customer groups, posted information on our
website, and initiated a public notice and comment period in the Federal Register in August 2025,
which concluded when the Postal Service published its final notice on this topic, including responses
to the comments received, in November 2025.
MYTH: Postmarks show when and where the Postal Service took possession of my mail
FACT: A postmark date does not necessarily indicate the first day that the Postal Service took
possession of the mailpiece. Rather, it confirms that the Postal Service accepted custody of a
mailpiece, and that the mailpiece was in the possession of the Postal Service on the identified date.

Ballot Mail for Federal Elections
• June 02, 2026 – Proposed rule filed in the Federal Register – Comment Period ended on July 2, 2026
• August 26, 2026 – Final Rule published in Federal Register
• Adds a new section to Domestic Mail Manual (DMM) in Section 705 “Advanced Preparation and Special
Postage Payment Systems.”
• The new rule establishes certain mail preparation and data-reporting requirements regarding absentee or
mail-in ballots for general, special, or run-off federal elections.
• These conditions do not apply to ballots for state elections only, ballots covered under the Uniformed and
Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act, or ballots for federal primary elections
• Based on the current litigation, for the November 3, 2026, elections the Postal Service is not permitted to
implement parts of the rule that require mandatory participation for envelope design, mailpiece design review,
or Federal Ballot Mail Portal use. The Postal Service is also barred from taking actions related to verification or
the potential non-acceptance of ballot mail.
